extraction.body: Google is making the Gemini AI assistant that’s already in millions of cars, trucks, and SUVs a lot more personal — a move that could push consumers even deeper into the company’s ecosystem of products. The company said Tuesday it’s upgrading Gemini in vehicles with a personal intelligence feature that can draw on information from Gmail, Google Calendar, YouTube, Maps, Google Search history, and other connected Google services to understand your preferences, activities, and past experiences. Google said it will roll out “Personal Intelligence with Gemini” to vehicles in two ways — through Android Auto, an app that runs on the user’s phone and wirelessly communicates with and projects navigation, media, and messaging to the vehicle’s infotainment system, and Google Built-in , software and services that have been directly integrated into the vehicle. The feature will launch in Android Auto, starting today, and expand to cars with Google Built-in in the coming months. Google initially launched Gemini last November in Android Auto. Meanwhile, Gemini’s “Personal Intelligence” feature rolled out across the U.S. in March and is now in beta in global markets. This latest upgrade would connect the dots — as Google put it in its blog post — across users’ Google apps. Drivers will have to opt in for Personalized Intelligence to work. Once a user does so, they should expect all sorts of cross-pollination. For instance, a driver who is navigating to the airport may be alerted that the flight on their calendar is delayed. Google said the feature will allow users to make complex requests using natural language. Returning to that airport example, a user might ask the AI assistant for their flight gate before quickly following up with a question about whether it’s still on time. Gemini will give the user answers to both questions at the same time, the company said. That level of emmeshing might make consumers uncomfortable, although Google says users do retain full control over their data with Personal Intelligence. The feature can be turned on or off at any time, and users can selectively choose which apps they’d like to connect, Google said. story.title: Google is bringing a more personal version of its Gemini AI assistant to your car

facts.text: Waymo has brought Gemini to its purpose-built Ojai vehicles to create a more helpful and personalized ride.
While the Waymo Driver safely navigates the roads, you can now use Gemini as an in-car AI assistant.
Just press the Gemini icon on the screen and use your voice to control the cabin or learn about your surroundings.
You can ask Gemini to “turn the A/C to 65,” find the best nearby coffee shop, or share the history of a local monument you're passing.
This new integration gives you hands-free control and a wealth of knowledge right from your seat.
Your Google Photos library could soon influence the kind of images you can generate with Gemini.

After letting users personalize the AI assistant's responses with data from Gmail, Search and YouTube, Google says it's bringing that same "Personal Intelligence" to Nano Banana 2 to make it easier for users to create personalized images with the AI model.

Rather than prompting Gemini's image generation model with information about you or photos of your belongings, a direction to "create a picture of my desert island essentials" should produce an image that includes the things you care about without any extra context.
Google says the feature will come to Gemini in Chrome and other users "soon."

Google is making the Gemini AI assistant that’s already in millions of cars, trucks, and SUVs a lot more personal — a move that could push consumers even deeper into the company’s ecosystem of products.
Google said the feature will allow users to make complex requests using natural language.
Gemini will give the user answers to both questions at the same time, the company said.

Google said it will roll out “Personal Intelligence with Gemini” to vehicles in two ways — through Android Auto, an app that runs on the user’s phone and wirelessly communicates with and projects navigation, media, and messaging to the vehicle’s infotainment system, and Google Built-in , software and services that have been directly integrated into the vehicle.
Google initially launched Gemini last November in Android Auto.
That level of emmeshing might make consumers uncomfortable, although Google says users do retain full control over their data with Personal Intelligence.
This latest upgrade would connect the dots — as Google put it in its blog post — across users’ Google apps.

sources.title: Samsung readies $648 billion bet, report says, as AI boom reshapes South Korea - Yahoo Finance
passages: SEOUL, June 26 (Reuters) - Samsung Group will unveil a sweeping decade-long investment plan on Monday, pledging 1,000 trillion won ($648 billion) to anchor South Korea's next growth cycle, ‌including a possible 300 trillion won push to build chip factories in the country's southwest, a media report ‌said.

At its core, the initiative appears designed to decentralise South Korea's AI boom ‌into a nationwide engine of growth, easing infrastructure ⁠bottlenecks while jumpstarting jobs, innovation hubs and next-generation manufacturing across underserved regions.

The regional politics ​surrounding semiconductor investment became a flashpoint ahead of South ​Korea's June 3 local elections, and debate over where the next wave of funding should go ‌has intensified as Lee's government has made AI a ​core economic policy priority.
Candidates across multiple regions aggressively pitched their areas as the next semiconductor hub, promising to lure giants such as ​Samsung and SK Hynix.

Presidential policy adviser Kim Yong-beom said on Wednesday that SK Hynix and Samsung may need to accelerate projects originally slated for the 2040s into the mid-2030s because AI-driven ‌memory demand was growing faster than expected, leaving no room, power ​or water in the capital region for subsequent expansion.

extraction.body: SEOUL, June 26 (Reuters) - Samsung Group will unveil a sweeping decade-long investment plan on Monday, pledging 1,000 trillion won ($648 billion) to anchor South Korea's next growth cycle, ‌including a possible 300 trillion won push to build chip factories in the country's southwest, a media report ‌said. The investment, which would include AI data centers, batteries and displays, will be announced at a meeting with President Lee Jae Myung at the presidential ​office, the Maeil Business Newspaper said on Friday, without citing sources. Top executives from heavyweights including Samsung Electronics and its rival SK Hynix will attend the meeting and lay out investment plans targeting regions beyond Seoul and its surrounding hubs, the report said. The report did not say when the investment would be made. At its core, the initiative appears designed to decentralise South Korea's AI boom ‌into a nationwide engine of growth, easing infrastructure ⁠bottlenecks while jumpstarting jobs, innovation hubs and next-generation manufacturing across underserved regions. The concentration of the chipmakers' production facilities in areas around Seoul has long drawn political pressure, and has been amplified by ⁠Lee's push for balanced regional development. Lee had separate meetings with the heads of Samsung and SK this week, media reports said. The presidential office said it will announce on Monday "three mega-projects" to drive a national leap forward, although it has not yet confirmed the content ​of ​the projects. Samsung Group is South ​Korea's biggest conglomerate, with chip giant Samsung Electronics as ‌its crown jewel, but also other affiliates such as battery maker Samsung SDI and IT services company Samsung SDS. A presidential adviser said this week that it is in talks with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix on the next phase of large-scale investments in semiconductor production facilities to meet exponential growth in AI-driven demand for chips. Presidential policy adviser Kim Yong-beom said on Wednesday that SK Hynix and Samsung may need to accelerate projects originally slated for the 2040s into the mid-2030s because AI-driven ‌memory demand was growing faster than expected, leaving no room, power ​or water in the capital region for subsequent expansion. The regional politics ​surrounding semiconductor investment became a flashpoint ahead of South ​Korea's June 3 local elections, and debate over where the next wave of funding should go ‌has intensified as Lee's government has made AI a ​core economic policy priority. Lee's approval ​rating has fallen to 51%, the lowest since his inauguration in June last year, Gallup Korea said on Friday. Candidates across multiple regions aggressively pitched their areas as the next semiconductor hub, promising to lure giants such as ​Samsung and SK Hynix. Proposals ranged from ‌a 500 trillion won chip complex in the southwest to expanded clusters in Gyeonggi, Chungcheong and Gangwon, according ​to local media, underscoring a nationwide contest for strategic tech investment.

The South Korean government has greenlit the Yongin Semiconductor National Industrial Complex three months earlier than expected, which will significantly reduce the project planning timeline, reports BusinessKorea . The science park is said to be the world's largest semiconductor hub, accommodating multiple fabs, power plants, and fab suppliers. The Yongin Semiconductor National Industrial Complex spans 7.28 square kilometers (equivalent to 1,020 soccer fields or 3.6 times the size of Monaco, or about half the size of Beverly Hills). sources.title: A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub
passages: Generative AI models run on powerful chips known as GPUs, which depend on stacks of specialized memory chips packaged with the processor.
To meet growing demand for memory, Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea.
Three fabs already operate around the clock, and a fourth is coming online.
Along with the cautionary messages, there’s a sense of urgency in the air.

And for years the company watched its domestic rival SK Hynix pull ahead in the global market for the high-bandwidth models that power Nvidia’s AI accelerators. (Meanwhile, the Taiwanese chipmaker TSMC has dominated the foundry business, manufacturing chips that other companies design.) The Pyeongtaek build-out is Samsung’s attempt to reclaim its lead on memory chips.
It’s just before noon on a Monday, and construction workers are pouring out of Samsung’s fabs in Pyeongtaek, a farming city south of Seoul where rice paddies abut a sprawling chipmaking complex.
Thousands of workers, dressed head to toe in black with sky-blue vests, take off helmets bearing their names and fab numbers.
They walk to lunch, sweaty and flushed, in chunky sneakers capped with yellow rubber toe guards.
Some hop on scooters or motorcycles to get around the campus, which covers an area about the size of New York City’s Central Park.
They’ll dine at buffets, diners, and beef stew joints, walking past banners advertising short-term leases for studio apartments.
Some stop by real estate offices to inquire, stepping up to the same counters where Samsung’s salaried engineers buy new homes .

extraction.body: At the world’s biggest chipmaking complex, Samsung is building the fabs it needs for the AI memory boom. Generative AI models run on powerful chips known as GPUs, which depend on stacks of specialized memory chips packaged with the processor. To meet growing demand for memory, Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea. Three fabs already operate around the clock, and a fourth is coming online. Construction of a fifth was halted during a drop in demand for memory chips in 2024 but restarted when the AI boom sent demand soaring. It’s just before noon on a Monday, and construction workers are pouring out of Samsung’s fabs in Pyeongtaek, a farming city south of Seoul where rice paddies abut a sprawling chipmaking complex. Thousands of workers, dressed head to toe in black with sky-blue vests, take off helmets bearing their names and fab numbers. They walk to lunch, sweaty and flushed, in chunky sneakers capped with yellow rubber toe guards. Some hop on scooters or motorcycles to get around the campus, which covers an area about the size of New York City’s Central Park. They’ll dine at buffets, diners, and beef stew joints, walking past banners advertising short-term leases for studio apartments. Some stop by real estate offices to inquire, stepping up to the same counters where Samsung’s salaried engineers buy new homes . In front of the fourth fab, I meet Choi Hye-rin, a 35-year-old safety officer, as she wipes her forehead with a handkerchief. At dawn, she boarded one of the shuttle buses that ferry workers in from Songtan, an older, scrappier district. She oversees the safety of a crew responsible for building cable ducts. She writes reports, inspects equipment, and checks the chemicals the workers handle. She’s one of hundreds of women working on site, many employed as spotters who walk ahead of heavy equipment. Safety is a big deal here. After lunch, construction picks right back up. Excavators move past rust-red steel structures rising high under tower cranes. Banners that hang from the highest girders read, “Even if the work runs late, don’t rush.” A giant LED scoreboard announces the winners of a contest for writing a poem about safety. Helmets stickered with a pledge, “I will not work if it’s not safe,” perch atop lockers. The finished fabs glisten from across the street. Along with the cautionary messages, there’s a sense of urgency in the air. Samsung predicts that demand for memory chips will continue to surge through 2028. And for years the company watched its domestic rival SK Hynix pull ahead in the global market for the high-bandwidth models that power Nvidia’s AI accelerators. (Meanwhile, the Taiwanese chipmaker TSMC has dominated the foundry business, manufacturing chips that other companies design.) The Pyeongtaek build-out is Samsung’s attempt to reclaim its lead on memory chips. Although the heat can be brutal and the work zones are crowded, Hye-rin has no plans to leave. “The rate here is higher than other construction sites, and the work is relatively easy,” she says. She gets paid 140,000 won ($97) a day and expects the boom to keep her busy for some time: “You just keep coming back.” Ten years after AlphaGo’s match against Go champion Lee Sedol, today’s AI still isn’t tapping into the machinery that made that win possible.

coreStoryFacts.text: SEOUL, June 26 (Reuters) - Samsung Group will unveil a sweeping decade-long investment plan on Monday, pledging 1,000 trillion won ($648 billion) to anchor South Korea's next growth cycle, ‌including a possible 300 trillion won push to build chip factories in the country's southwest, a media report ‌said.

At its core, the initiative appears designed to decentralise South Korea's AI boom ‌into a nationwide engine of growth, easing infrastructure ⁠bottlenecks while jumpstarting jobs, innovation hubs and next-generation manufacturing across underserved regions.

The regional politics ​surrounding semiconductor investment became a flashpoint ahead of South ​Korea's June 3 local elections, and debate over where the next wave of funding should go ‌has intensified as Lee's government has made AI a ​core economic policy priority.
Candidates across multiple regions aggressively pitched their areas as the next semiconductor hub, promising to lure giants such as ​Samsung and SK Hynix.

Presidential policy adviser Kim Yong-beom said on Wednesday that SK Hynix and Samsung may need to accelerate projects originally slated for the 2040s into the mid-2030s because AI-driven ‌memory demand was growing faster than expected, leaving no room, power ​or water in the capital region for subsequent expansion.
Electronics giant Samsung says it plans to invest around 300tn won ($230.8bn; £189.6bn) over 20 years in the South Korea government's push to develop a mega semiconductor hub in the country.
"The mega cluster will be the key base of our semiconductor ecosystem," South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy said in a statement on Wednesday .
South Korea is home to other major microprocessor manufacturers such as SK Hynix.
This will be put towards building five chip factories, the firm told the BBC.
Samsung is the world's biggest maker of memory chips, smartphones and TVs.

The science park is said to be the world's largest semiconductor hub, accommodating multiple fabs, power plants, and fab suppliers.

Lee had separate meetings with the heads of Samsung and SK this week, media reports said. The presidential office said it will announce on Monday "three mega-projects" to drive a national leap forward, although it has not yet confirmed the content ​of ​the projects. Samsung Group is South ​Korea's biggest conglomerate, with chip giant Samsung Electronics as ‌its crown jewel, but also other affiliates such as battery maker Samsung SDI and IT services company Samsung SDS. A presidential adviser said this week that it is in talks with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix on the next phase of large-scale investments in semiconductor production facilities to meet exponential growth in AI-driven demand for chips. Presidential policy adviser Kim Yong-beom said on Wednesday that SK Hynix and Samsung may need to accelerate projects originally slated for the 2040s into the mid-2030s because AI-driven ‌memory demand was growing faster than expected, leaving no room, power ​or water in the capital region for subsequent expansion. The regional politics ​surrounding semiconductor investment became a flashpoint ahead of South ​Korea's June 3 local elections, and debate over where the next wave of funding should go ‌has intensified as Lee's government has made AI a ​core economic policy priority. Lee's approval ​rating has fallen to 51%, the lowest since his inauguration in June last year, Gallup Korea said on Friday. Candidates across multiple regions aggressively pitched their areas as the next semiconductor hub, promising to lure giants such as ​Samsung and SK Hynix. Proposals ranged from ‌a 500 trillion won chip complex in the southwest to expanded clusters in Gyeonggi, Chungcheong and Gangwon, according ​to local media, underscoring a nationwide contest for strategic tech investment.

The South Korean government has greenlit the Yongin Semiconductor National Industrial Complex three months earlier than expected, which will significantly reduce the project planning timeline, reports BusinessKorea . The science park is said to be the world's largest semiconductor hub, accommodating multiple fabs, power plants, and fab suppliers. The Yongin Semiconductor National Industrial Complex spans 7.28 square kilometers (equivalent to 1,020 soccer fields or 3.6 times the size of Monaco, or about half the size of Beverly Hills). It will feature six major semiconductor fabrication plants, three power plants, and 60 small and medium-sized enterprises specializing in materials, parts, and equipment necessary to keep the fabs operating. The first semiconductor plant in YSNIC is expected to begin operations by 2030. Bringing together major makers of microelectronics — such as Samsung and SK hynix — and their suppliers in one large Yongin Semiconductor Cluster is a smart move from the South Korean government as it will enable close collaboration between chipmakers and their suppliers, which might speed up the development of new process technologies and/or shrinking time-to-yield. The report says that the Yongin Cluster complex aims to attract private investments totaling 300 trillion won ($203.75 billion), generate an estimated 1.6 million jobs, and add 700 trillion won ($475.41 billion) in production value once completed. ConstructionThe construction of the Yongin Cluster, initially planned for 2029, will begin in December 2026, a leap forward of three and a half years. To do so, the Korean government expedited land compensation processes, which are set to start next year, and intends to expand critical infrastructure like roads, water, and electricity as soon as possible. In addition to its industrial scope, the complex will include residential areas, creating a small mixed-use city. The approval ceremony occurred at Samsung Electronics' Giheung Campus in Gyeonggi Province on December 26. The event brought together key participants, including Samsung Electronics and SK hynix and representatives from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, and Transport, Gyeonggi Province, Yongin City, Korea Land and Housing Corporation (LH). During the gathering, officials unveiled a detailed development blueprint for the Yongin Semiconductor National Industrial Complex to highlight the government's dedication to advancing the country's semiconductor sector. Generative AI models run on powerful chips known as GPUs, which depend on stacks of specialized memory chips packaged with the processor. To meet growing demand for memory, Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea. Three fabs already operate around the clock, and a fourth is coming online. Construction of a fifth was halted during a drop in demand for memory chips in 2024 but restarted when the AI boom sent demand soaring. It’s just before noon on a Monday, and construction workers are pouring out of Samsung’s fabs in Pyeongtaek, a farming city south of Seoul where rice paddies abut a sprawling chipmaking complex. Thousands of workers, dressed head to toe in black with sky-blue vests, take off helmets bearing their names and fab numbers. They walk to lunch, sweaty and flushed, in chunky sneakers capped with yellow rubber toe guards. Some hop on scooters or motorcycles to get around the campus, which covers an area about the size of New York City’s Central Park. They’ll dine at buffets, diners, and beef stew joints, walking past banners advertising short-term leases for studio apartments. Some stop by real estate offices to inquire, stepping up to the same counters where Samsung’s salaried engineers buy new homes . In front of the fourth fab, I meet Choi Hye-rin, a 35-year-old safety officer, as she wipes her forehead with a handkerchief. At dawn, she boarded one of the shuttle buses that ferry workers in from Songtan, an older, scrappier district. She oversees the safety of a crew responsible for building cable ducts. She writes reports, inspects equipment, and checks the chemicals the workers handle. She’s one of hundreds of women working on site, many employed as spotters who walk ahead of heavy equipment. Safety is a big deal here. After lunch, construction picks right back up. Excavators move past rust-red steel structures rising high under tower cranes. Banners that hang from the highest girders read, “Even if the work runs late, don’t rush.” A giant LED scoreboard announces the winners of a contest for writing a poem about safety. Helmets stickered with a pledge, “I will not work if it’s not safe,” perch atop lockers. The finished fabs glisten from across the street. Along with the cautionary messages, there’s a sense of urgency in the air. Samsung predicts that demand for memory chips will continue to surge through 2028. And for years the company watched its domestic rival SK Hynix pull ahead in the global market for the high-bandwidth models that power Nvidia’s AI accelerators. (Meanwhile, the Taiwanese chipmaker TSMC has dominated the foundry business, manufacturing chips that other companies design.) It’s just before noon on a Monday, and construction workers are pouring out of Samsung’s fabs in Pyeongtaek, a farming city south of Seoul where rice paddies abut a sprawling chipmaking complex. Thousands of workers, dressed head to toe in black with sky-blue vests, take off helmets bearing their names and fab numbers.

They walk to lunch, sweaty and flushed, in chunky sneakers capped with yellow rubber toe guards. Some hop on scooters or motorcycles to get around the campus, which covers an area about the size of New York City’s Central Park. They’ll dine at buffets, diners, and beef stew joints, walking past banners advertising short-term leases for studio apartments. Some stop by real estate offices to inquire, stepping up to the same counters where Samsung’s salaried engineers buy new homes .

In front of the fourth fab, I meet Choi Hye-rin, a 35-year-old safety officer, as she wipes her forehead with a handkerchief. At dawn, she boarded one of the shuttle buses that ferry workers in from Songtan, an older, scrappier district. She oversees the safety of a crew responsible for building cable ducts. story.title: A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub

facts.text: SEOUL, June 26 (Reuters) - Samsung Group will unveil a sweeping decade-long investment plan on Monday, pledging 1,000 trillion won ($648 billion) to anchor South Korea's next growth cycle, ‌including a possible 300 trillion won push to build chip factories in the country's southwest, a media report ‌said.
Candidates across multiple regions aggressively pitched their areas as the next semiconductor hub, promising to lure giants such as ​Samsung and SK Hynix.

Presidential policy adviser Kim Yong-beom said on Wednesday that SK Hynix and Samsung may need to accelerate projects originally slated for the 2040s into the mid-2030s because AI-driven ‌memory demand was growing faster than expected, leaving no room, power ​or water in the capital region for subsequent expansion.
Electronics giant Samsung says it plans to invest around 300tn won ($230.8bn; £189.6bn) over 20 years in the South Korea government's push to develop a mega semiconductor hub in the country.
"The mega cluster will be the key base of our semiconductor ecosystem," South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy said in a statement on Wednesday .
South Korea is home to other major microprocessor manufacturers such as SK Hynix.
This will be put towards building five chip factories, the firm told the BBC.
Samsung is the world's biggest maker of memory chips, smartphones and TVs.

The South Korean government has greenlit the Yongin Semiconductor National Industrial Complex three months earlier than expected, which will significantly reduce the project planning timeline, reports BusinessKorea .
The science park is said to be the world's largest semiconductor hub, accommodating multiple fabs, power plants, and fab suppliers.

The smart ring space is heating up, and we have officially reached peak health tracker.
I’ve tested the device for months now, and it surpasses the competition by a mile.
The impressive software comes to both models through the app.

Another reason to buy the new ring could be the (somewhat) extended battery life, if your Ring 3’s battery is withering away, and the expanded sizing if you haven’t found a smart ring that fits your finger.
No smart ring is as innovative, feature-rich, size-inclusive, and thoughtful in its design and rollout.
I put the ring on at 9 am on a Friday morning, and somewhere between Wednesday night and Thursday morning, the ring hit 0% and died on me.
Oura adds 10 extra signal pathways, making 18 in total to gather health data and adjust for the natural movements of the ring that occur during daily wear.
Also: Your next Oura Ring or Apple watch could have a feature that transforms healthcare
Also: Oura surpasses Apple Watch and Fitbit’s sleep accuracy in recent study
Oura has redesigned the interface to create three core tabs: Today, Vitals, and My Health.
The Today tab provides a snapshot of your daily scores and health data, like readiness, sleep, activity, heart rate, and stress duration.
You’ll also pay $6 monthly if you want access to all the data the ring gathers.
It’s the most competitive and innovative wearable within the space right now.
Oura puts comfort at the forefront of its Ring 4 — both functional comfort, being great to wear, and via extended and inclusive sizing.
Let’s start with heart rate monitoring.
The upgraded app — available to all Oura users, regardless of smart ring generation — takes this data automatically when it detects movement.
When dancing at a concert one night, the device automatically clocked the activity and recorded my heart rate.
I love any feature upgrade that does the busy work for me, so I can spend less time thinking about recording my activities and more time doing the activity itself (and reviewing the data later).
I wore the Gen 3 for most of last year, and I regularly noticed dry spots around my finger where the protruded sensor domes left impressions.
This made the device irritating to wear for longer periods.

An Oura spokesperson recommended disabling the blood oxygen sensing feature and updating to the latest software to improve battery life, and this gave me an extra few days with the ring before recharging.
That said, copycats always follow the innovators, and we’re seeing some competitors implementing Oura’s features, like its Cardiovascular Age and Daytime Stress features, into their own products.
Lastly, Oura upgraded its daytime stress feature by including the tags users add throughout the day and the exercises it automatically detects and overlays on the daytime stress timeline.

extraction.body: The Oura Ring 4 is a powerful sleep and health tracker with a discreet build and endless features for further understanding your health. While Oura was quiet these past few years, in between the release of its Ring 3 in 2021 and the development of its Ring 4 (now available) , a groundswell of competitors released smart rings of their own, from big-name brands like Samsung to indie upstarts like Ultrahuman and RingConn. Also: Oura’s CEO wants its smart ring to be the doctor in your pocket The smart ring space is heating up, and we have officially reached peak health tracker. During the past few years, Oura has been busy developing a smart ring that’s smarter and stronger than the rest: the recently unveiled Oura Ring 4 . I’ve tested the device for months now, and it surpasses the competition by a mile. Here’s how. The Oura Ring 4 improves upon the battery life, comfort, and software features of its predecessor. It’s $50 more expensive than the Oura Ring 3, but comes with smarter sensors and a thinner build. Oura puts comfort at the forefront of its Ring 4 — both functional comfort, being great to wear, and via extended and inclusive sizing. Oura’s Ring 3 offers sizes six through 13, and the Ring 4 offers sizes four through 15. Out of all the smart rings I’ve tested on the market, this sizing range is the most expansive and will fit finger sizes small and large. I wore the Gen 3 for most of last year, and I regularly noticed dry spots around my finger where the protruded sensor domes left impressions. This made the device irritating to wear for longer periods. The Ring 4 uses recessed smart sensors to keep the inside of the ring flat and easy to wear, creating the most comfortable and unnoticeable generation of the device yet. The Oura Ring 4 (left) has receded sensors that make it more comfortable to wear compared to Oura Ring 3 (right). A major selling point that intrigued me with the Oura Ring 4 is the extended and uber-competitive eight-day battery life. I hadn’t seen any competing smart rings with such a long battery life, so I was eager to see how long the device would last. I put the ring on at 9 am on a Friday morning, and somewhere between Wednesday night and Thursday morning, the ring hit 0% and died on me. That battery life clocked in at about five days, three days less than advertised. An Oura spokesperson recommended disabling the blood oxygen sensing feature and updating to the latest software to improve battery life, and this gave me an extra few days with the ring before recharging. Most batteries don’t last as long as advertised for regular wear. For example, Samsung’s Galaxy Ring advertises a seven-day battery life but regularly lasts four to five days, tops. On the bright side, recharging the ring took no time and boosted the battery from 0% to 30% in less than 20 minutes. Also: Oura Ring 3 vs Oura Ring 4: Should you buy the discounted smart ring or the brand’s newest? Another major selling point of the Oura Ring 4 is its smart sensors, which keep the build comfortable and its battery life long. Oura adds 10 extra signal pathways, making 18 in total to gather health data and adjust for the natural movements of the ring that occur during daily wear. Hardware aside, the software inside the app is as intriguing and updated as the physical ring itself. Some of my favorite features Oura improves upon in its fourth-generation device include the automatic heart rate monitoring that takes place through its workout detection feature, the meal-logging functionality that correctly cataloged my slop of a breakfast (more on that later), and the daytime stress feature that offers more context than ever. Also: Your next Oura Ring or Apple watch could have a feature that transforms healthcare Let’s start with heart rate monitoring. Before the Ring 4 upgrade, if you wanted to capture data on your heart rate while exercising, you’d have to go into the app to hit record on that function. The upgraded app — available to all Oura users, regardless of smart ring generation — takes this data automatically when it detects movement. When dancing at a concert one night, the device automatically clocked the activity and recorded my heart rate. I love any feature upgrade that does the busy work for me, so I can spend less time thinking about recording my activities and more time doing the activity itself (and reviewing the data later). Oura Ring 4 could accurately detect what was in my hodge-podge of a yogurt bowl. You can’t count calories with this feature; instead, it’s a way to log the timing of your meals to understand how regularity impacts your vitals over the day. Meal logging is an experimental feature and could disappear in time, but it’s a helpful and impressive tool that utilizes AI cleverly and surprisingly. Also: Oura surpasses Apple Watch and Fitbit’s sleep accuracy in recent study Lastly, Oura upgraded its daytime stress feature by including the tags users add throughout the day and the exercises it automatically detects and overlays on the daytime stress timeline. The overlaid timeline clarifies and distinguishes between bodily stress caused by a hard workout or stress caused by a day at work or a social outing late at night. You can see tags for when you undergo physiological stress, such as activity overlaid on the daytime timeline. The October launch of the Ring 4 also brings the Oura app redesign. Given the smart ring is screenless, the user experience relies on an effective app with great data illustration. Oura has redesigned the interface to create three core tabs: Today, Vitals, and My Health. The Today tab provides a snapshot of your daily scores and health data, like readiness, sleep, activity, heart rate, and stress duration. The Vitals tab shows you a historical view of those scores. The My Health tab shows trends that don’t change over a week or two, like your resilience level, cardiovascular age , and sleep health. The layout is a thoughtful way to separate the many datasets Oura records into relevant-by-day, relevant-by-week, and longitudinal illustrations. Some metrics are harder to find through this reorganization than others. Reddit users have already shared their critiques of the redesign, with many opposing these changes (it’s a universal tech truth that users rarely welcome an app redesign). With some curiosity and patience, you can still find the data you’re looking for on the app — trust me. Also: The Oura Ring 4 is ZDNET’s best product of the year As usual, you learn lots about your body simply by having this thing around your finger, such as how much better you sleep when you haven’t drunk alcohol or eaten late into the night, and how your body reacts to the daily stresses of being a human. That capability hasn’t changed from ring generation to generation. Another thing that, unfortunately, hasn’t changed is that this device will still cost you a lot of money — and you will still have to pay a monthly subscription (despite smart ring competitors doing away with subscriptions of their own). The Oura Ring 4 starts at $350 and rises depending on your desired finish. You’ll also pay $6 monthly if you want access to all the data the ring gathers. So, should you buy it? If I were to create the Oura Ring 4’s ideal customer, it would be someone who has the money (or the FSA/HSA funds, since the smart ring is FSA/HSA-eligible) and the curiosity to dive into their health insights and make lifestyle choices accordingly. This smart ring provides data-driven recommendations on sleep, activity, and stress to people who continually check the app. It’s helped me get my sleep in check and increase my activity, because I was incentivized to wear it and get my resilience and sleep regularity scores up. I can without a doubt confirm that it’s made my habits healthier — or brought my unhealthy habits to light, at the very least. The smart ring is constantly innovating with experimental features for metabolic, heart, and sleep health, so Oura Ring 4’s ideal customer would be someone looking for groundbreaking features to use and experiment with. That said, copycats always follow the innovators, and we’re seeing some competitors implementing Oura’s features, like its Cardiovascular Age and Daytime Stress features, into their own products. The closest dupe is through subscription-free Ultrahuman Ring Air , and if you don’t want to pay the $6 a month subscription to have access to extensive health data, I’d recommend the Ring Air instead. Most of the hardware upgrades prioritize comfort, so if you already have an Oura Ring 3, I’d only buy the Oura Ring 4 if you can’t stand the uncomfortable protruding dome sensors of the earlier generation. The impressive software comes to both models through the app. Another reason to buy the new ring could be the (somewhat) extended battery life, if your Ring 3’s battery is withering away, and the expanded sizing if you haven’t found a smart ring that fits your finger. If you haven’t purchased a smart ring yet, I’d recommend the Ring 4 . Despite its competitors vying for attention, there’s no question which company is winning the smart-ring race — and it’s the Oura Ring 4 . No smart ring is as innovative, feature-rich, size-inclusive, and thoughtful in its design and rollout. The Oura Ring 4’s impressive and accurate suite of health tracking features is an example of technology working to its fullest effect. Oura has innovated within the health wearables space, and the smart ring that started as a health tracker has shifted to become a helpful health assistant, thanks to features and data accuracy that encourage healthy behaviors and spot abnormalities. It’s the most competitive and innovative wearable within the space right now. Please accept cookies to view the comments powered by Disqus.

Reddit users have already shared their critiques of the redesign, with many opposing these changes (it’s a universal tech truth that users rarely welcome an app redesign). With some curiosity and patience, you can still find the data you’re looking for on the app — trust me.

As usual, you learn lots about your body simply by having this thing around your finger, such as how much better you sleep when you haven’t drunk alcohol or eaten late into the night, and how your body reacts to the daily stresses of being a human. That capability hasn’t changed from ring generation to generation.

Another thing that, unfortunately, hasn’t changed is that this device will still cost you a lot of money — and you will still have to pay a monthly subscription (despite smart ring competitors doing away with subscriptions of their own). The Oura Ring 4 starts at $350 and rises depending on your desired finish. You’ll also pay $6 monthly if you want access to all the data the ring gathers.

So, should you buy it? If I were to create the Oura Ring 4’s ideal customer, it would be someone who has the money (or the FSA/HSA funds, since the smart ring is FSA/HSA-eligible) and the curiosity to dive into their health insights and make lifestyle choices accordingly.

This smart ring provides data-driven recommendations on sleep, activity, and stress to people who continually check the app. It’s helped me get my sleep in check and increase my activity, because I was incentivized to wear it and get my resilience and sleep regularity scores up. I can without a doubt confirm that it’s made my habits healthier — or brought my unhealthy habits to light, at the very least.

The smart ring is constantly innovating with experimental features for metabolic, heart, and sleep health, so Oura Ring 4’s ideal customer would be someone looking for groundbreaking features to use and experiment with.

That said, copycats always follow the innovators, and we’re seeing some competitors implementing Oura’s features, like its Cardiovascular Age and Daytime Stress features, into their own products. The closest dupe is through subscription-free Ultrahuman Ring Air , and if you don’t want to pay the $6 a month subscription to have access to extensive health data, I’d recommend the Ring Air instead.

Most of the hardware upgrades prioritize comfort, so if you already have an Oura Ring 3, I’d only buy the Oura Ring 4 if you can’t stand the uncomfortable protruding dome sensors of the earlier generation. The impressive software comes to both models through the app. Another reason to buy the new ring could be the (somewhat) extended battery life, if your Ring 3’s battery is withering away, and the expanded sizing if you haven’t found a smart ring that fits your finger.

If you haven’t purchased a smart ring yet, I’d recommend the Ring 4 . Despite its competitors vying for attention, there’s no question which company is winning the smart-ring race — and it’s the Oura Ring 4 . No smart ring is as innovative, feature-rich, size-inclusive, and thoughtful in its design and rollout.

The Oura Ring 4’s impressive and accurate suite of health tracking features is an example of technology working to its fullest effect. Oura has innovated within the health wearables space, and the smart ring that started as a health tracker has shifted to become a helpful health assistant, thanks to features and data accuracy that encourage healthy behaviors and spot abnormalities. It’s the most competitive and innovative wearable within the space right now.

sources.title: Oura adds new fitness metrics to show how workouts impact your body - TechCrunch
passages: As competition in the smart ring market escalates , Oura is introducing two new features to give people more insight into their workouts and how they impact their bodies.
The company announced on Tuesday it’s rolling out Cardio Effort and VO₂ max metrics to expand workout tracking beyond exercise duration and heart rate zones.
With Cardio Effort, users will be able to see how much a workout taxes their cardiovascular system.
This measurement is aggregated over the week relative to each user’s individual baseline to provide more insights.
Oura explained that this metric shifts users’ focus from “How many minutes did I move?” to “Am I maintaining my fitness, building it, or overdoing it?”
As for VO₂ max, the metric shows how workouts contribute to long-term fitness.
It measures how effectively the heart, lungs, and muscles work together to deliver and use oxygen during exercise.
Previously, measuring VO₂ max typically required a lab test or a six-minute walking test.
Oura can now estimate it passively using GPS-enabled workouts.
The first metric evaluates the impact of an individual workout, while the latter aggregates effort into a weekly total, categorized as “Light,” “Fair,” “Maintaining,” “Building,” or “Reaching.”
By launching more advanced workout metrics, Oura is looking to differentiate itself from competitors.

sources.title: Oura’s New Ring 5 Is Smaller and Lighter—and Adds an AI Health Coach
passages: Oura is positioning the Ring 5 as a proactive health platform, much like how Google is positioning its AI Health Coach at the center of the redesigned Google Health app.
Tiny Ring, Big Ambitions At 6.09 mm wide and 2.28 mm thick, Oura's latest ring is 40 percent smaller than the Ring 4, which the company claims makes it the world’s smallest smart ring.
Then there's Oura's preventive health ambitions: Health Radar, which builds on the Symptom Radar feature introduced in 2024.

Earlier this month, Oura announced a partnership with Resmed that offers users with elevated nighttime breathing alerts access to sleep health resources, complete sleep assessments, and the option to connect with independent healthcare providers for potential diagnosis and treatment.
Also new is multi-ring support, allowing users to pair and switch between multiple Ring 4 and Ring 5 devices on a single account at no additional charge.
The ring, charging case, and Oura membership all qualify for HSA and FSA reimbursement in the US.
Oura is also expanding its Health Panels feature with Lab Uploads, so you can import blood test results and compare biomarkers over time.
Oura is introducing GLP-1 medication self-management tools that allow users to log and track dosing schedules, side effects, and weight changes.
The new launch comes with a stronger emphasis on privacy controls, according to Oura.
The company is partnering with Counsel Health to integrate AI-assisted health guidance with access to licensed physicians through Oura Advisor.
Oura also says its updated Automatic Activity Detection is significantly more accurate than previous generations, particularly for lower-motion exercises like pilates.
Oura says this metric may reveal cardiovascular risks that daytime readings may miss.
A new time-based Data Deletion feature lets users—across all Oura generations—erase data from specific periods without wiping their long-term history.
Shrinking the Oura Ring hasn’t come at the expense of performance.

Oura is also expanding its Health Panels feature with Lab Uploads, so you can import blood test results and compare biomarkers over time. In the US, subscribers can connect eligible providers to import diagnosed conditions, medications, and lab results into a Personal Health Record in the app. The new launch comes with a stronger emphasis on privacy controls, according to Oura. A new time-based Data Deletion feature lets users—across all Oura generations—erase data from specific periods without wiping their long-term history. Members also have more granular oversight with configurable controls over how their data is used and shared with third parties. sources.title: Oura adds two new cardiovascular health tracking features to its smart rings
passages: Oura is introducing two new cardiovascular-focused health tracking features to its smart rings designed to help users better understand the effect regular workouts and exercise are having on their long-term health, and whether they need to ramp it up or dial things down.

Oura Rings already support VO2 Max readings that are used to track aerobic capacity, but the previous Cardio Capacity feature was somewhat cumbersome because estimating a user’s maximum oxygen uptake required a six-minute walking test for calibration.

One one end of the scale is a Light rating that’s described as being a “substantially lower cardiovascular strain than your usual baseline.” The rating scale progresses through Fair, Maintaining, Building, and Reaching at the other end which means your weekly Cardio Effort had a “markedly higher exposure relative to your baseline, signaling that it may be time to prioritize recovery.” So instead of always pushing a user to increase their efforts, the feature does make recommendations for rest when it may be more beneficial.

The new version, automatic VO2 Max, currently available as a beta feature through Oura Labs, automatically activates after users complete five “qualifying GPS-enabled activities” that include walks, runs, and hikes.

coreStoryFacts.text: Also: The Oura Ring 4 is ZDNET’s best product of the year
The smart ring space is heating up, and we have officially reached peak health tracker.
I’ve tested the device for months now, and it surpasses the competition by a mile.
The impressive software comes to both models through the app.

Another reason to buy the new ring could be the (somewhat) extended battery life, if your Ring 3’s battery is withering away, and the expanded sizing if you haven’t found a smart ring that fits your finger.
No smart ring is as innovative, feature-rich, size-inclusive, and thoughtful in its design and rollout.
I put the ring on at 9 am on a Friday morning, and somewhere between Wednesday night and Thursday morning, the ring hit 0% and died on me.
Oura adds 10 extra signal pathways, making 18 in total to gather health data and adjust for the natural movements of the ring that occur during daily wear.
Also: Your next Oura Ring or Apple watch could have a feature that transforms healthcare
Also: Oura surpasses Apple Watch and Fitbit’s sleep accuracy in recent study
Oura has redesigned the interface to create three core tabs: Today, Vitals, and My Health.
The Today tab provides a snapshot of your daily scores and health data, like readiness, sleep, activity, heart rate, and stress duration.
You’ll also pay $6 monthly if you want access to all the data the ring gathers.
It’s the most competitive and innovative wearable within the space right now.
Oura puts comfort at the forefront of its Ring 4 — both functional comfort, being great to wear, and via extended and inclusive sizing.
Let’s start with heart rate monitoring.
The upgraded app — available to all Oura users, regardless of smart ring generation — takes this data automatically when it detects movement.
When dancing at a concert one night, the device automatically clocked the activity and recorded my heart rate.
I love any feature upgrade that does the busy work for me, so I can spend less time thinking about recording my activities and more time doing the activity itself (and reviewing the data later).
I wore the Gen 3 for most of last year, and I regularly noticed dry spots around my finger where the protruded sensor domes left impressions.

An Oura spokesperson recommended disabling the blood oxygen sensing feature and updating to the latest software to improve battery life, and this gave me an extra few days with the ring before recharging.
That said, copycats always follow the innovators, and we’re seeing some competitors implementing Oura’s features, like its Cardiovascular Age and Daytime Stress features, into their own products.

Then there's Oura's preventive health ambitions: Health Radar, which builds on the Symptom Radar feature introduced in 2024.

Earlier this month, Oura announced a partnership with Resmed that offers users with elevated nighttime breathing alerts access to sleep health resources, complete sleep assessments, and the option to connect with independent healthcare providers for potential diagnosis and treatment.
Also new is multi-ring support, allowing users to pair and switch between multiple Ring 4 and Ring 5 devices on a single account at no additional charge.
The ring, charging case, and Oura membership all qualify for HSA and FSA reimbursement in the US.
Oura is also expanding its Health Panels feature with Lab Uploads, so you can import blood test results and compare biomarkers over time.
Oura is introducing GLP-1 medication self-management tools that allow users to log and track dosing schedules, side effects, and weight changes.
The new launch comes with a stronger emphasis on privacy controls, according to Oura.
The company is partnering with Counsel Health to integrate AI-assisted health guidance with access to licensed physicians through Oura Advisor.
Oura also says its updated Automatic Activity Detection is significantly more accurate than previous generations, particularly for lower-motion exercises like pilates.
Oura says this metric may reveal cardiovascular risks that daytime readings may miss.
A new time-based Data Deletion feature lets users—across all Oura generations—erase data from specific periods without wiping their long-term history.
Shrinking the Oura Ring hasn’t come at the expense of performance.

Oura is introducing two new cardiovascular-focused health tracking features to its smart rings designed to help users better understand the effect regular workouts and exercise are having on their long-term health, and whether they need to ramp it up or dial things down.

Oura Rings already support VO2 Max readings that are used to track aerobic capacity, but the previous Cardio Capacity feature was somewhat cumbersome because estimating a user’s maximum oxygen uptake required a six-minute walking test for calibration.

One one end of the scale is a Light rating that’s described as being a “substantially lower cardiovascular strain than your usual baseline.” The rating scale progresses through Fair, Maintaining, Building, and Reaching at the other end which means your weekly Cardio Effort had a “markedly higher exposure relative to your baseline, signaling that it may be time to prioritize recovery.” So instead of always pushing a user to increase their efforts, the feature does make recommendations for rest when it may be more beneficial.

The new version, automatic VO2 Max, currently available as a beta feature through Oura Labs, automatically activates after users complete five “qualifying GPS-enabled activities” that include walks, runs, and hikes.

The Oura Ring 4 (left) has receded sensors that make it more comfortable to wear compared to Oura Ring 3 (right). I hadn’t seen any competing smart rings with such a long battery life, so I was eager to see how long the device would last. I put the ring on at 9 am on a Friday morning, and somewhere between Wednesday night and Thursday morning, the ring hit 0% and died on me. An Oura spokesperson recommended disabling the blood oxygen sensing feature and updating to the latest software to improve battery life, and this gave me an extra few days with the ring before recharging. sources.title: Oura adds new fitness metrics to show how workouts impact your body - TechCrunch
passages: As competition in the smart ring market escalates , Oura is introducing two new features to give people more insight into their workouts and how they impact their bodies.
The company announced on Tuesday it’s rolling out Cardio Effort and VO₂ max metrics to expand workout tracking beyond exercise duration and heart rate zones.
With Cardio Effort, users will be able to see how much a workout taxes their cardiovascular system.
This measurement is aggregated over the week relative to each user’s individual baseline to provide more insights.
Oura explained that this metric shifts users’ focus from “How many minutes did I move?” to “Am I maintaining my fitness, building it, or overdoing it?”
As for VO₂ max, the metric shows how workouts contribute to long-term fitness.
It measures how effectively the heart, lungs, and muscles work together to deliver and use oxygen during exercise.
Previously, measuring VO₂ max typically required a lab test or a six-minute walking test.
Oura can now estimate it passively using GPS-enabled workouts.
The first metric evaluates the impact of an individual workout, while the latter aggregates effort into a weekly total, categorized as “Light,” “Fair,” “Maintaining,” “Building,” or “Reaching.”
By launching more advanced workout metrics, Oura is looking to differentiate itself from competitors.

sources.title: Oura’s New Ring 5 Is Smaller and Lighter—and Adds an AI Health Coach
passages: Oura is positioning the Ring 5 as a proactive health platform, much like how Google is positioning its AI Health Coach at the center of the redesigned Google Health app.
Tiny Ring, Big Ambitions At 6.09 mm wide and 2.28 mm thick, Oura's latest ring is 40 percent smaller than the Ring 4, which the company claims makes it the world’s smallest smart ring.
Then there's Oura's preventive health ambitions: Health Radar, which builds on the Symptom Radar feature introduced in 2024.

Earlier this month, Oura announced a partnership with Resmed that offers users with elevated nighttime breathing alerts access to sleep health resources, complete sleep assessments, and the option to connect with independent healthcare providers for potential diagnosis and treatment.
Also new is multi-ring support, allowing users to pair and switch between multiple Ring 4 and Ring 5 devices on a single account at no additional charge.
The ring, charging case, and Oura membership all qualify for HSA and FSA reimbursement in the US.
Oura is also expanding its Health Panels feature with Lab Uploads, so you can import blood test results and compare biomarkers over time.
Oura is introducing GLP-1 medication self-management tools that allow users to log and track dosing schedules, side effects, and weight changes.
The new launch comes with a stronger emphasis on privacy controls, according to Oura.
The company is partnering with Counsel Health to integrate AI-assisted health guidance with access to licensed physicians through Oura Advisor.
Oura also says its updated Automatic Activity Detection is significantly more accurate than previous generations, particularly for lower-motion exercises like pilates.
Oura says this metric may reveal cardiovascular risks that daytime readings may miss.
A new time-based Data Deletion feature lets users—across all Oura generations—erase data from specific periods without wiping their long-term history.
Shrinking the Oura Ring hasn’t come at the expense of performance.

Shrinking the Oura Ring hasn’t come at the expense of performance. Oura says the Ring 5 is more accurate than its predecessor, thanks to LEDs four times more powerful and redesigned sensors positioned closer to the skin for improved signal detection. The ring supposedly incorporates 12 independent signal pathways to refine accuracy across a range of finger shapes and skin tones. Battery life gets a modest boost, too, with Oura claiming between six and nine days per charge, up from the Ring 4’s five-to-eight-day range. Oura is also releasing a new portable Charging Case ($99), which can add an extra month of battery life, or roughly five full charges. It’s also compatible with the new Locate feature rolling out to Gen 2 devices and newer, allowing users to track misplaced rings and charging cases through the Oura app. The Oura Advisor The most notable changes arrive on the software side. Oura is positioning the Ring 5 as a proactive health platform, much like how Google is positioning its AI Health Coach at the center of the redesigned Google Health app. Central to that shift is Oura Advisor, the company’s large-language-model-powered assistant that debuted last year, and Oura’s proprietary AI model for women’s health. The company is partnering with Counsel Health to integrate AI-assisted health guidance with access to licensed physicians through Oura Advisor. Via the integration, you can ask health questions, receive personalized guidance, and connect with health care professionals from the app. A new live activity mode lets users start workouts from the app and view heart rate, pace, and distance in real time through lock-screen widgets, so you don't even have to unlock your phone mid-session. For activities where a smart ring can be uncomfortable, such as powerlifting, the app now supports third-party heart-rate monitors and select devices, so you can continue to capture live workout data without wearing the ring itself. Oura also says its updated Automatic Activity Detection is significantly more accurate than previous generations, particularly for lower-motion exercises like pilates. Then there's Oura's preventive health ambitions: Health Radar, which builds on the Symptom Radar feature introduced in 2024. Health Radar continuously analyzes biometric patterns in the background to flag subtle changes before they become more obvious problems. At launch, Health Radar centers around two new functions: Blood Pressure Signals and Nighttime Breathing. Blood Pressure Signals continuously analyzes biometric trends that may correlate with cardiovascular strain. Oura says this metric may reveal cardiovascular risks that daytime readings may miss. Earlier this month, Oura announced a partnership with Resmed that offers users with elevated nighttime breathing alerts access to sleep health resources, complete sleep assessments, and the option to connect with independent healthcare providers for potential diagnosis and treatment. Oura is introducing GLP-1 medication self-management tools that allow users to log and track dosing schedules, side effects, and weight changes. Oura is also expanding its Health Panels feature with Lab Uploads, so you can import blood test results and compare biomarkers over time. In the US, subscribers can connect eligible providers to import diagnosed conditions, medications, and lab results into a Personal Health Record in the app. The new launch comes with a stronger emphasis on privacy controls, according to Oura. A new time-based Data Deletion feature lets users—across all Oura generations—erase data from specific periods without wiping their long-term history. Members also have more granular oversight with configurable controls over how their data is used and shared with third parties. The Ring 5 is available in sizes 6 through 13, and Oura recommends all consumers, including existing members, use the company’s updated sizing kit before ordering, since the smaller design may fit differently than previous generations. Also new is multi-ring support, allowing users to pair and switch between multiple Ring 4 and Ring 5 devices on a single account at no additional charge.

sources.title: Oura adds two new cardiovascular health tracking features to its smart rings
passages: Oura is introducing two new cardiovascular-focused health tracking features to its smart rings designed to help users better understand the effect regular workouts and exercise are having on their long-term health, and whether they need to ramp it up or dial things down.

Oura Rings already support VO2 Max readings that are used to track aerobic capacity, but the previous Cardio Capacity feature was somewhat cumbersome because estimating a user’s maximum oxygen uptake required a six-minute walking test for calibration.

One one end of the scale is a Light rating that’s described as being a “substantially lower cardiovascular strain than your usual baseline.” The rating scale progresses through Fair, Maintaining, Building, and Reaching at the other end which means your weekly Cardio Effort had a “markedly higher exposure relative to your baseline, signaling that it may be time to prioritize recovery.” So instead of always pushing a user to increase their efforts, the feature does make recommendations for rest when it may be more beneficial.

The new version, automatic VO2 Max, currently available as a beta feature through Oura Labs, automatically activates after users complete five “qualifying GPS-enabled activities” that include walks, runs, and hikes.

passages: Depositions of employees filed in March 2026 are shedding new light on TikTok's child safety practices.
TikTok was repeatedly warned by employees about the risks the social media platform posed to children, according to court records obtained by NPR .
The documents say employees were frustrated with how executives responded to their concerns about risks to children, including sexual exploitation and exposure to suicide-related content.

According to NPR, TikTok employees warned that minors were appearing in sexual content that was available for purchase on TikTok, raising concerns that the company could profit from potentially illegal activity.
TikTok, in addition to Meta, Google, and Snap, faces hundreds of lawsuits consolidated in federal court.
The lawsuits allege that these companies' platforms harm minors and that they failed to disclose known risks to young users.

"These citations and claims are clearly cherry-picked at the behest of trial lawyers and used to inaccurately rewrite our history and mislead the public about our commitment to youth safety and how our platform works," a TikTok spokesperson said in an emailed statement to TechCrunch.
"It's unfortunate that NPR has chosen to ignore the numerous documents and resources we have provided that demonstrate how these claims mischaracterize our record and platform features."
Additionally, the court documents show that TikTok didn't conduct surveys to determine the age of its users out of concern that it would have to share the results with the Federal Trade Commission.
PT: The article was updated to include a statement from TikTok.

passages: TikTok employees repeatedly raised concerns internally about the risks the short-form video app posed to children, including sexual exploitation and exposure to suicide content.
Previously unreported court records show that the employees were frustrated with how the company's leadership responded to their concerns.
Depositions of staffers filed in federal court in March 2026 offer new insights into how TikTok has approached child safety since the platform exploded in popularity among young users in 2018.
Employees raised the alarm about minors appearing in sexual content on the app, which viewers could pay to access and the company would profit from — a potential financial crime.
TikTok also refrained from conducting surveys to assess the ages of its users because it was concerned that it would have to turn the results over to the Federal Trade Commission, the documents show.
NPR repeatedly sought comment from TikTok about the issues raised in the court documents.

Maher stated the company was aware of the sexual exploitation of minors on the platform before the Forbes article was published. The company did not respond to NPR's questions about its anti-money laundering protocols, including whether it filed suspicious activity reports to the Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network related to the revenues it received from TikTok Live videos containing illegal material. The app first became prominent in 2018, when ByteDance, TikTok's parent company, acquired Musical.ly, a platform for creating short music and lip-syncing videos that was popular with teen users in the U.S. Musical.ly was combined with TikTok, triggering rapid growth in the app's international user base. Because of this, the survey avoided questions that could point to users' ages, such as what phase of schooling users were enrolled in. COPPA is a federal law that protects the online privacy and personal information of children under 13. It generally prohibits companies from collecting children's personal information without verifiable parental consent. TikTok said it notifies parents' accounts when a minor unlinks from family pairing. Among the most serious concerns raised in the testimony was TikTok's handling of content related to suicide and self-harm for young users. Testimony from Eric Han , who was TikTok's head of safety from April 2019 through June 2023, detailed internal chats he'd engaged in concerning "rabbit holes" — the company's term for when the algorithm gets stuck showing the user the same type of content over and over again. Han said he became aware of this problem in April 2020, and acknowledged that rabbit holes could be harmful, such as ones focusing on body image or suicide, and could violate TikTok's policies. An internal report authored and circulated by Han in 2020 and discussed in his testimony stated that there is a "Real contagion effect. Suicidal ideation and behavior, and the way that it is talked about on the platform." In a draft of TikTok's 2020 "Minor Safety Policy Annual Review", which was also quoted in Han's deposition, included bullet points stating: "Social media is inherently dangerous, and all minors are at risk when they engage on the platform" and "Minor Safety is an urgent issue that we must address effectively." Despite this, Han said the platform did not warn parents of the potential dangers of TikTok.

coreStoryFacts.text: Depositions of employees filed in March 2026 are shedding new light on TikTok's child safety practices.
TikTok was repeatedly warned by employees about the risks the social media platform posed to children, according to court records obtained by NPR .
The documents say employees were frustrated with how executives responded to their concerns about risks to children, including sexual exploitation and exposure to suicide-related content.

According to NPR, TikTok employees warned that minors were appearing in sexual content that was available for purchase on TikTok, raising concerns that the company could profit from potentially illegal activity.
TikTok, in addition to Meta, Google, and Snap, faces hundreds of lawsuits consolidated in federal court.
The lawsuits allege that these companies' platforms harm minors and that they failed to disclose known risks to young users.

"These citations and claims are clearly cherry-picked at the behest of trial lawyers and used to inaccurately rewrite our history and mislead the public about our commitment to youth safety and how our platform works," a TikTok spokesperson said in an emailed statement to TechCrunch.
"It's unfortunate that NPR has chosen to ignore the numerous documents and resources we have provided that demonstrate how these claims mischaracterize our record and platform features."
Additionally, the court documents show that TikTok didn't conduct surveys to determine the age of its users out of concern that it would have to share the results with the Federal Trade Commission.

According to NPR, TikTok employees warned that minors were appearing in sexual content that was available for purchase on TikTok, raising concerns that the company could profit from potentially illegal activity. They also flagged that minors were exploiting loopholes to access age-restricted content and hide their activity from parents. Additionally, the court documents show that TikTok didn't conduct surveys to determine the age of its users out of concern that it would have to share the results with the Federal Trade Commission. "These citations and claims are clearly cherry-picked at the behest of trial lawyers and used to inaccurately rewrite our history and mislead the public about our commitment to youth safety and how our platform works," a TikTok spokesperson said in an emailed statement to TechCrunch. "It's unfortunate that NPR has chosen to ignore the numerous documents and resources we have provided that demonstrate how these claims mischaracterize our record and platform features." The statement continues, "We have invested billions of dollars in Trust & Safety and rolled out more than 50 preset safety, privacy, and security settings for teens, including Family Pairing, which helps parents and guardians customize the experience for their teens. We remain steadfast in our commitment to the well-being of our community." TikTok, in addition to Meta, Google, and Snap, faces hundreds of lawsuits consolidated in federal court. The lawsuits allege that these companies' platforms harm minors and that they failed to disclose known risks to young users. sources.title: TikTok staff raised child safety alarms. Court records show executives failed to act - NPR
passages: TikTok employees repeatedly raised concerns internally about the risks the short-form video app posed to children, including sexual exploitation and exposure to suicide content.
Previously unreported court records show that the employees were frustrated with how the company's leadership responded to their concerns.
Depositions of staffers filed in federal court in March 2026 offer new insights into how TikTok has approached child safety since the platform exploded in popularity among young users in 2018.
Employees raised the alarm about minors appearing in sexual content on the app, which viewers could pay to access and the company would profit from — a potential financial crime.
TikTok also refrained from conducting surveys to assess the ages of its users because it was concerned that it would have to turn the results over to the Federal Trade Commission, the documents show.
NPR repeatedly sought comment from TikTok about the issues raised in the court documents.
After extended communications, the company initially declined to provide a statement for this story.
It did, however, direct NPR to various company policies that it had previously published on its website.

In one deposition , Reagen Maher, who held senior roles in safety and investigations at TikTok between 2021 and 2024, described going on a "crusade" for several months trying to elevate safety issues with some of TikTok's highest executives.
Maher testified that her findings had been escalated to V Pappas, TikTok's chief operating officer at the time.

The company did not respond to NPR's questions about its anti-money laundering protocols, including whether it filed suspicious activity reports to the Treasury Department's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network related to the revenues it received from TikTok Live videos containing illegal material.
Because the cases against TikTok have yet to be heard before a jury, the previously unreported employee depositions reviewed by NPR have not been submitted as evidence at trial.

In 2024, NPR reported on improperly redacted documents from another legal case that revealed that company employees sought to maximize teenagers' use of the app even while it publicly backed screentime limits for younger users.

In a draft of TikTok's 2020 "Minor Safety Policy Annual Review", which was also quoted in Han's deposition, included bullet points stating: "Social media is inherently dangerous, and all minors are at risk when they engage on the platform" and "Minor Safety is an urgent issue that we must address effectively."
The report identified risks including adult predators grooming children and the creation of child sexual abuse material.
It also found that TikTok received "significant revenue" from gifts sent to livestreams that violated the platform's rules.

After publication, TikTok spokesperson Nathaniel Brown sent a statement saying the citations and claims in the story are "clearly cherry-picked at the behest of trial lawyers and used to inaccurately rewrite our history and mislead the public about our commitment to youth safety and how our platform works."

In 2021, TikTok introduced age-based account settings that restrict some features for 13 to 17-year-olds, including limits on sending and receiving direct messages and broadcasting in real time on TikTok Live.

Musical.ly was combined with TikTok, triggering rapid growth in the app's international user base. (As of January 22, 2026, TikTok's U.S. operations are majority-owned by American investors, following a deal that reduced ByteDance's control over the platform.)
They noted that "Having elementary school [as an answer in the survey] is definitely violating COPPA [the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act]," Wang confirmed in his testimony.
Because of this, the survey avoided questions that could point to users' ages, such as what phase of schooling users were enrolled in.
In an ongoing lawsuit filed in 2024, Utah's attorney general alleged that TikTok's Live feature exposed minors to sexual exploitation by adults, while TikTok profited from the transactions.
Other employee testimony highlighted TikTok's difficulties in preventing users under 18 from accessing adult-only features and harmful content.
TikTok said it notifies parents' accounts when a minor unlinks from family pairing.
