passages: Justin Mast’s life was changed by a cyborg plant.

A few years ago, Mast was reading through some scientific literature when he stumbled upon research about a houseplant wired to a motorized stand . When the plant wanted more light, electrical signals flowed through the living tissues. A control board sensed the current and wheeled the plant closer to the light source.
“I’m like, what the heck?” Mast told TechCrunch. “That was the entry to the rabbit hole for me.”

Mast wound up partnering with Lee von Kraus, a neuroscientist who has worked with DARPA, to found Electric Plant , which has been spending the past three years collecting data to build a large language model, Bombadil, capable of interpreting the subtle electrical signals coursing through a plant’s stem and relaying details about the plant’s needs to growers.

The founders believe their model could one day lead to a tool that would let people “speak” to plants. “We’re listening more than we’re speaking, but listening’s the first step,” said Mast, co-founder and CEO of Electric Plant.

To bring its sensors and Bombadil to market, Electric Plant recently raised an $11.2 million seed round led by Onto Ventures and Climactic, with participation from Ponderosa, Endeavor Catalyst, Ludlow, Michigan Rise, The Fund, Schox VC, and Dug Song.

Even in the most controlled greenhouses, farmers and growers don’t have full visibility of what their plants require, Mast said. Traditionally, farmers, growers, and foresters have relied on coarse tools that react to plants’ demands for water, nutrients, or light. And tools like soil probes, handheld spectroscopes, and satellite imagery work well enough, but they leave much to be desired, Mast said.

“That technology is sophisticated, but its ability to get at the inside of the plant isn’t very sophisticated. Most of that stuff still lags quite a bit behind the real-time needs of the plant,” he said.

Electric Plant had to start somewhere, though, so it used those devices to train its Bombadil model, which is capable of interpreting electrical signals in about 125 different species. “We know the model will surpass a lot of that equipment,” Mast said.
The startup’s sensors are also significantly cheaper than existing tools, which generally cost thousands of dollars. “This is tens of dollars,” he said.

The sensors, about the size of a regular iPhone folded lengthwise, are attached to a plant using stainless steel screws. The screws must penetrate the cambium — the layer of living tissue just under the bark — to connect to the microvolt changes occurring within the plant. Data collected from these sensors is sent to a base station via a low-power wireless network.

Electric Plant only needs a couple sensors per acre for accurate results, Mast said. The data gets interpreted by Bombadil in the cloud, and the results are sent back to the customer, who can use it to, for example, adjust their watering or fertilizer schedules. Mast claims such a system can boost yields while reducing water use by 20% or more.
Mast wouldn’t disclose who Electric Plant’s initial customers are, but it’s easy to imagine applications in agriculture and forestry.
Bombadil’s first hundred-plus species runs the gamut of plant forms, from ferns, redwoods, and tomatoes to dahlias, Mast said.
“This is the most diverse model ever created on biological electrical signals,” he said. “No one’s ever done anything equivalent to this in the animal world.”

passages: Bill Gates said he’s prepared to plow billions of dollars into a next-generation nuclear power plant project in Wyoming to meet growing US electricity needs.

TerraPower LLC, a startup founded by Gates, broke ground for construction of its first commercial reactor last week in Wyoming, where a coal plant is shutting down, the billionaire co-founder of Microsoft Corp. said on CBS’s Face the Nation . TerraPower has explored simpler, cheaper reactors since 2008 and expects to complete the new reactor in 2030. “I put in over a billion, and I’ll put in billions more,” said Gates, the world’s sixth-richest person according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. TerraPower’s plant, which has backing by the US Department of Energy, was initially expected to be operational in 2028. But that would have meant relying on fuel from Russia, which is “unacceptable now,” Gates said on CNN’s Fareed Zakaria GPS . The reactor design uses liquid sodium as a coolant rather than water and includes molten salt that can store heat to boost its output. TerraPower plans to source reactor fuel from the US and its allies, Gates said. “Coal is being outcompeted by natural gas,” Gates told CNN. “And so what we have to do is compete effectively with natural gas.” Carbon-free nuclear power is increasingly seen as a key part of fighting climate change, and more companies are promoting smaller reactors. Last year, 25 nations at the COP28 climate change conference in Dubai declared an ambition to triple nuclear capacity, according to BloombergNEF.

passages: 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Aikido Security today announced the launch of Noon , a dedicated workforce security business that extends its protection beyond software to the people using it.
AI has made sophisticated phishing, deepfakes and coordinated social engineering attacks cheaper, easier to execute and more scalable than ever before.
Noon addresses these threats by bringing email protection, device protection, AI governance and phishing simulation training together in one platform.
"We started Aikido to make securing software radically simpler," said Willem Delbare, CEO of Aikido Security.
"But companies don't just need to protect the software they build.
With Noon, we're bringing the same approach to workforce security: one platform, less complexity, and protection for every employee, not just those building software."

Noon's platform is being built on two acquisitions Aikido completed in September 2026: Poland-based Cyberly, founded in 2024, which brought AI-driven attack simulations and AI usage visibility, and Belgium-based Outkept, founded in 2020, which brought email security and phishing awareness training.
Before the acquisitions, Cyberly protected more than 300,000 employees across 200-plus organizations, while Outkept served more than 1,000 organizations and 250,000 users across 100-plus countries.
"AI has fundamentally changed how we need to train and protect employees.
"Joining forces with Cyberly and Aikido gives us the opportunity to rethink workforce security and bring a new generation of protection to organizations of all sizes."
Aikido's unified security platform secures application testing, code, cloud and runtime, helping teams to reduce risk without slowing down development.

Aikido is the fastest-ever European cybersecurity company to reach unicorn status and is trusted by over 150,000 teams, with a global customer base including SoundCloud, Niantic, Runway, Handshake and Deel.
Noon brings employee security into one platform, replacing the separate tools many organizations piece together today:
Aikido Security achieves FedRAMP Moderate Authorization, bringing AI-native, automated vulnerability remediation to U.S. federal agencies.
Yet the security industry has long treated software and workforce security as two separate worlds," said Alex Horlach, co-founder of Cyberly.
The founding teams of both companies continue at Noon.
Cyberly's four co-founders, Alex Horlach, Evgeny Chamtonau, Pavel Hraznykh and Andrew Labadzinski, will continue building the platform.

Together, Cyberly and Outkept bring established international customer relationships and a strong foundation for Noon's growth, with additional opportunities across Aikido's existing customer network.
Most workforce security stacks were built for a different problem: generic phishing emails and scheduled tests.
They also run separately from the tools protecting employee devices or tracking AI usage, leaving security teams managing several disconnected products.
Noon connects directly to Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Slack and Microsoft Teams, and its results are built to feed into GRC platforms.
Campaign and training data is designed to support audits under frameworks including SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIS2, DORA, HIPAA and GDPR, and to help meet cyber insurance requirements.
Aikido achieves AWS Security Competency for Application Security, giving AWS customers independent validation of its code-to-cloud-to-runtime platform.

coreStoryFacts.text: 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Aikido Security today announced the launch of Noon , a dedicated workforce security business that extends its protection beyond software to the people using it.
AI has made sophisticated phishing, deepfakes and coordinated social engineering attacks cheaper, easier to execute and more scalable than ever before.
Noon addresses these threats by bringing email protection, device protection, AI governance and phishing simulation training together in one platform.
"We started Aikido to make securing software radically simpler," said Willem Delbare, CEO of Aikido Security.
"But companies don't just need to protect the software they build.
With Noon, we're bringing the same approach to workforce security: one platform, less complexity, and protection for every employee, not just those building software."

Noon's platform is being built on two acquisitions Aikido completed in September 2026: Poland-based Cyberly, founded in 2024, which brought AI-driven attack simulations and AI usage visibility, and Belgium-based Outkept, founded in 2020, which brought email security and phishing awareness training.
Before the acquisitions, Cyberly protected more than 300,000 employees across 200-plus organizations, while Outkept served more than 1,000 organizations and 250,000 users across 100-plus countries.
"AI has fundamentally changed how we need to train and protect employees.
"Joining forces with Cyberly and Aikido gives us the opportunity to rethink workforce security and bring a new generation of protection to organizations of all sizes."
Aikido's unified security platform secures application testing, code, cloud and runtime, helping teams to reduce risk without slowing down development.

Aikido is the fastest-ever European cybersecurity company to reach unicorn status and is trusted by over 150,000 teams, with a global customer base including SoundCloud, Niantic, Runway, Handshake and Deel.
Noon brings employee security into one platform, replacing the separate tools many organizations piece together today:
Aikido Security achieves FedRAMP Moderate Authorization, bringing AI-native, automated vulnerability remediation to U.S. federal agencies.
Yet the security industry has long treated software and workforce security as two separate worlds," said Alex Horlach, co-founder of Cyberly.
The founding teams of both companies continue at Noon.
Cyberly's four co-founders, Alex Horlach, Evgeny Chamtonau, Pavel Hraznykh and Andrew Labadzinski, will continue building the platform.

Together, Cyberly and Outkept bring established international customer relationships and a strong foundation for Noon's growth, with additional opportunities across Aikido's existing customer network.
Most workforce security stacks were built for a different problem: generic phishing emails and scheduled tests.
They also run separately from the tools protecting employee devices or tracking AI usage, leaving security teams managing several disconnected products.
Noon connects directly to Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Slack and Microsoft Teams, and its results are built to feed into GRC platforms.
Campaign and training data is designed to support audits under frameworks including SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIS2, DORA, HIPAA and GDPR, and to help meet cyber insurance requirements.
Aikido achieves AWS Security Competency for Application Security, giving AWS customers independent validation of its code-to-cloud-to-runtime platform.
“Aikido has already changed how companies secure their software.

extraction.body: Visa has partnered with crypto payments infrastructure provider Mesh to let consumers spend cryptocurrency and stablecoin balances at more than 175 million merchant locations worldwide without first transferring funds to a bank account or loading a separate payment card. Visa has partnered with Mesh to enable crypto and stablecoin spending at more than 175 million merchant locations across over 200 countries and territories. Consumers will be able to pay directly from supported wallet balances without cashing out, transferring funds or obtaining separate payment cards. Mesh will handle transaction funding and conversion, while merchants continue receiving payments through Visa's existing infrastructure. Participating platforms can offer the service through a single Mesh integration, with the company managing onboarding and customer verification. Initial availability, supported devices and participating crypto wallets have yet to be announced. 19 announcement, Mesh said the partnership would connect digital wallets and cryptocurrency platforms to Visa's payment network through its transaction processing infrastructure, allowing users to make purchases directly from their existing balances. The proposed service will support payments at physical stores and online merchants across more than 200 countries and territories where Visa operates. Mesh will handle the conversion and movement of funds behind each transaction, while merchants receive payments through their existing checkout systems. Visa processed $14.2 trillion in payment volume during fiscal 2025, according to figures cited in the announcement. Visa and Mesh will connect crypto wallets to existing payment terminals Under the agreement, Mesh will allow participating wallet providers and cryptocurrency platforms to offer payments directly from digital asset balances without requiring customers to withdraw their holdings before making a purchase. The payment process will rely on a Visa credential created in the background. Mesh will manage the funding and conversion process when a transaction takes place, drawing from supported cryptocurrency, stablecoin or fiat balances. Merchants will continue receiving payments through Visa's existing infrastructure, without installing new hardware or changing how they accept transactions. The arrangement does not mean merchants will receive cryptocurrency directly. Mesh will handle the conversion required to complete payments through the conventional payment network. According to the company, wallet providers can activate the service through a single Mesh integration without developing and operating their own card programs. Mesh will act as the program manager and handle customer onboarding and know your customer checks associated with the service. The company said its network already serves more than 200 enterprises and connects hundreds of wallets, exchanges and financial platforms. Its existing enterprise relationships include Kalshi, Tools for Humanity, Félix Pago, Majority and KAST, although the announcement did not confirm which partners would participate in the initial Visa rollout. "Crypto never had a spending problem, it has a last-mile problem," Mesh co-founder and CEO Bam Azizi said in the announcement. Azizi said the company's infrastructure would manage funding and conversion at the time of payment, removing the need for customers to move money between accounts before making purchases. Visa's global head of growth, Rubail Birwadker, said the collaboration would give consumers more ways to use digital asset balances through established payment services. Visa expands stablecoin payments beyond dedicated card programs The partnership follows several initiatives by Visa to connect cryptocurrency holdings and stablecoin transactions with its existing payments infrastructure. In September, Visa disclosed that more than 160 stablecoin card programs were operating globally during its fiscal second quarter of 2026. Payment volume across those programs had climbed nearly 200% from the previous year, while the company's stablecoin settlement business surpassed an annualized rate of $20 billion. An October update showed that stablecoin card payments continued to record nearly 200% annual growth across Visa's network. Business and commercial programs accounted for approximately 17% of the company's stablecoin-linked card payment volume during fiscal 2026. The Mesh arrangement uses a different customer-facing model from conventional cryptocurrency card programs because participating platforms can provide payment access without requiring customers to obtain a separate card associated with each wallet. Earlier payment integrations have generally required users to convert cryptocurrency into fiat before spending it or rely on dedicated cards issued through specific providers. In January, Visa partnered with Mercuryo to allow eligible users to convert cryptocurrency into fiat and transfer the proceeds to Visa debit and credit cards through Visa Direct. The service was designed to deliver funds to eligible cards within minutes, depending on the supported market and payment conditions. Visa entered another digital asset agreement in October when it partnered with ADI Foundation to explore blockchain infrastructure and digital payment systems. That agreement remained exploratory, with neither company announcing a specific blockchain, stablecoin or commercial launch date. Mesh builds on existing exchange and stablecoin integrations Mesh has spent much of 2026 adding cryptocurrency exchanges, wallets and payment platforms to its network. In September, crypto.news reported that Bybit Pay integrated Mesh to connect its payment service with more than 300 wallets, exchanges and financial platforms.

Mesh and Visa ( NYSE:V | V Price Prediction ) have teamed up to let users spend crypto and stablecoin balances held in wallet apps at more than 175 million merchants worldwide, without needing a separate crypto card. The company announced this significant development on October 19, 2026. Many crypto holders have never spent their digital assets in stores. Until now, converting crypto to cash often required selling coins, waiting for the funds to transfer to a bank, or signing up for a crypto debit card linked to a specific exchange. While the checkout process is straightforward under this new arrangement, tax considerations can catch new users off guard. Here’s what to expect at checkout and what tax implications may follow. The wallet app takes care of most of the payment process. According to the announcement, the participating wallet app sets up a Visa card behind the scenes. Users can tap a standard contactless terminal or check out online without selling, transferring, or preloading any funds. When it’s time to pay, Mesh determines how the purchase is funded—crypto, a stablecoin (a token designed to maintain a steady $1 value), or regular dollars. The merchant receives the payment as a standard Visa transaction, requiring no additional hardware and ensuring cashiers see a typical card payment. Mesh has not yet specified which cryptocurrencies it will support, any applicable fees, or which countries it will include in the initial rollout. Users should check their wallet apps to confirm three critical details before buying. The IRS classifies cryptocurrencies as property. As a result, spending crypto is a taxable event, similar to selling it. The IRS states that “an exchange of digital assets for property, goods, or services” constitutes a taxable transaction. According to Form 1040 instructions, you must report any disposal through payment on Form 8949 and Schedule D. For instance, if someone purchases a $1,000 laptop using Bitcoin bought at $500, they owe taxes on the $500 gain , even if they haven’t converted any crypto to cash. At the 15% long-term capital gains rate (for assets held over a year), the laptop adds about $75 to their tax bill. Coins held for a year or less are taxed at the regular income tax rate, which is usually higher. Additionally, a purchase can lock in a loss. For example, if Bitcoin trades at about $81,000 , down from $111,000 a year earlier, selling coins bought at the higher price would realize a capital loss that could offset other capital gains. Stablecoins largely avoid these complexities, as tokens like USD Coin ( CRYPTO:USDC ) usually maintain a value close to $1. However, these transactions still count as disposals, and the IRS requires taxpayers to keep detailed records of every sale, exchange, or disposal of virtual currency and its fair market value. Mesh and Visa’s new setup benefits individuals who hold stablecoins, receive payments in them, or frequently make cross-border transactions and prefer to spend directly without cashing out first. Stablecoins simplify tax tracking and suit everyday purchases. However, long-term crypto holders may find it more advantageous to keep their investments separate and use a traditional card for payments. Tax tracking is the cost. Each purchase with a coin that has risen in value may create a gain to report. Small purchases add up fast over a year, so frequent spenders of appreciated coins will likely require tax software. If Mesh and its partners publish clear coin and fee lists at launch, this could become one of the easiest ways to spend crypto—as long as users know the tax owed on each transaction. Many crypto holders have never spent their digital assets in stores. Until now, converting crypto to cash often required selling coins, waiting for the funds to transfer to a bank, or signing up for a crypto debit card linked to a specific exchange.
While the checkout process is straightforward under this new arrangement, tax considerations can catch new users off guard. Here’s what to expect at checkout and what tax implications may follow.

The wallet app takes care of most of the payment process. According to the announcement, the participating wallet app sets up a Visa card behind the scenes. Users can tap a standard contactless terminal or check out online without selling, transferring, or preloading any funds.

When it’s time to pay, Mesh determines how the purchase is funded—crypto, a stablecoin (a token designed to maintain a steady $1 value), or regular dollars. The merchant receives the payment as a standard Visa transaction, requiring no additional hardware and ensuring cashiers see a typical card payment.

Mesh has not yet specified which cryptocurrencies it will support, any applicable fees, or which countries it will include in the initial rollout. Users should check their wallet apps to confirm three critical details before buying.

The IRS classifies cryptocurrencies as property. As a result, spending crypto is a taxable event, similar to selling it. The IRS states that “an exchange of digital assets for property, goods, or services” constitutes a taxable transaction. According to Form 1040 instructions, you must report any disposal through payment on Form 8949 and Schedule D.

For instance, if someone purchases a $1,000 laptop using Bitcoin bought at $500, they owe taxes on the $500 gain , even if they haven’t converted any crypto to cash. At the 15% long-term capital gains rate (for assets held over a year), the laptop adds about $75 to their tax bill. Coins held for a year or less are taxed at the regular income tax rate, which is usually higher.

Additionally, a purchase can lock in a loss. For example, if Bitcoin trades at about $81,000 , down from $111,000 a year earlier, selling coins bought at the higher price would realize a capital loss that could offset other capital gains.

Stablecoins largely avoid these complexities, as tokens like USD Coin ( CRYPTO:USDC ) usually maintain a value close to $1. However, these transactions still count as disposals, and the IRS requires taxpayers to keep detailed records of every sale, exchange, or disposal of virtual currency and its fair market value.

Mesh and Visa’s new setup benefits individuals who hold stablecoins, receive payments in them, or frequently make cross-border transactions and prefer to spend directly without cashing out first. Stablecoins simplify tax tracking and suit everyday purchases. However, long-term crypto holders may find it more advantageous to keep their investments separate and use a traditional card for payments.

Tax tracking is the cost. Each purchase with a coin that has risen in value may create a gain to report. Small purchases add up fast over a year, so frequent spenders of appreciated coins will likely require tax software. If Mesh and its partners publish clear coin and fee lists at launch, this could become one of the easiest ways to spend crypto—as long as users know the tax owed on each transaction.

extraction.body: Visa has partnered with crypto payments infrastructure provider Mesh to let consumers spend cryptocurrency and stablecoin balances at more than 175 million merchant locations worldwide without first transferring funds to a bank account or loading a separate payment card. Visa has partnered with Mesh to enable crypto and stablecoin spending at more than 175 million merchant locations across over 200 countries and territories. Consumers will be able to pay directly from supported wallet balances without cashing out, transferring funds or obtaining separate payment cards. Mesh will handle transaction funding and conversion, while merchants continue receiving payments through Visa's existing infrastructure. Participating platforms can offer the service through a single Mesh integration, with the company managing onboarding and customer verification. Initial availability, supported devices and participating crypto wallets have yet to be announced. 19 announcement, Mesh said the partnership would connect digital wallets and cryptocurrency platforms to Visa's payment network through its transaction processing infrastructure, allowing users to make purchases directly from their existing balances. The proposed service will support payments at physical stores and online merchants across more than 200 countries and territories where Visa operates. Mesh will handle the conversion and movement of funds behind each transaction, while merchants receive payments through their existing checkout systems. Visa processed $14.2 trillion in payment volume during fiscal 2025, according to figures cited in the announcement. Visa and Mesh will connect crypto wallets to existing payment terminals Under the agreement, Mesh will allow participating wallet providers and cryptocurrency platforms to offer payments directly from digital asset balances without requiring customers to withdraw their holdings before making a purchase. The payment process will rely on a Visa credential created in the background. Mesh will manage the funding and conversion process when a transaction takes place, drawing from supported cryptocurrency, stablecoin or fiat balances. Merchants will continue receiving payments through Visa's existing infrastructure, without installing new hardware or changing how they accept transactions. The arrangement does not mean merchants will receive cryptocurrency directly. Mesh will handle the conversion required to complete payments through the conventional payment network. According to the company, wallet providers can activate the service through a single Mesh integration without developing and operating their own card programs. Mesh will act as the program manager and handle customer onboarding and know your customer checks associated with the service. The company said its network already serves more than 200 enterprises and connects hundreds of wallets, exchanges and financial platforms. Its existing enterprise relationships include Kalshi, Tools for Humanity, Félix Pago, Majority and KAST, although the announcement did not confirm which partners would participate in the initial Visa rollout. "Crypto never had a spending problem, it has a last-mile problem," Mesh co-founder and CEO Bam Azizi said in the announcement. Azizi said the company's infrastructure would manage funding and conversion at the time of payment, removing the need for customers to move money between accounts before making purchases. Visa's global head of growth, Rubail Birwadker, said the collaboration would give consumers more ways to use digital asset balances through established payment services. Visa expands stablecoin payments beyond dedicated card programs The partnership follows several initiatives by Visa to connect cryptocurrency holdings and stablecoin transactions with its existing payments infrastructure. In September, Visa disclosed that more than 160 stablecoin card programs were operating globally during its fiscal second quarter of 2026. Payment volume across those programs had climbed nearly 200% from the previous year, while the company's stablecoin settlement business surpassed an annualized rate of $20 billion. An October update showed that stablecoin card payments continued to record nearly 200% annual growth across Visa's network. Business and commercial programs accounted for approximately 17% of the company's stablecoin-linked card payment volume during fiscal 2026. The Mesh arrangement uses a different customer-facing model from conventional cryptocurrency card programs because participating platforms can provide payment access without requiring customers to obtain a separate card associated with each wallet. Earlier payment integrations have generally required users to convert cryptocurrency into fiat before spending it or rely on dedicated cards issued through specific providers. extraction.body: Visa just opened 175 million merchants to crypto spenders, but the real catch has nothing to do with card readers or wallet apps. Every tap at checkout could quietly trigger a tax bill most users never see coming. It sounds nuts, but SoFi is giving new Active Invest users up to $1,000 in stock for a limited time, and all it takes is a $50 deposit to get started. Mesh and Visa ( NYSE:V | V Price Prediction ) have teamed up to let users spend crypto and stablecoin balances held in wallet apps at more than 175 million merchants worldwide, without needing a separate crypto card. The company announced this significant development on October 19, 2026. Many crypto holders have never spent their digital assets in stores. Until now, converting crypto to cash often required selling coins, waiting for the funds to transfer to a bank, or signing up for a crypto debit card linked to a specific exchange. While the checkout process is straightforward under this new arrangement, tax considerations can catch new users off guard. Here’s what to expect at checkout and what tax implications may follow. The wallet app takes care of most of the payment process. According to the announcement, the participating wallet app sets up a Visa card behind the scenes. Users can tap a standard contactless terminal or check out online without selling, transferring, or preloading any funds. When it’s time to pay, Mesh determines how the purchase is funded—crypto, a stablecoin (a token designed to maintain a steady $1 value), or regular dollars. The merchant receives the payment as a standard Visa transaction, requiring no additional hardware and ensuring cashiers see a typical card payment. "Fishpool gold coins" by Lawrence OP is licensed under BY 2.0. Mesh has not yet specified which cryptocurrencies it will support, any applicable fees, or which countries it will include in the initial rollout. Users should check their wallet apps to confirm three critical details before buying. The IRS classifies cryptocurrencies as property. As a result, spending crypto is a taxable event, similar to selling it. The IRS states that “an exchange of digital assets for property, goods, or services” constitutes a taxable transaction. According to Form 1040 instructions, you must report any disposal through payment on Form 8949 and Schedule D. For instance, if someone purchases a $1,000 laptop using Bitcoin bought at $500, they owe taxes on the $500 gain , even if they haven’t converted any crypto to cash. At the 15% long-term capital gains rate (for assets held over a year), the laptop adds about $75 to their tax bill. Coins held for a year or less are taxed at the regular income tax rate, which is usually higher. Additionally, a purchase can lock in a loss. For example, if Bitcoin trades at about $81,000 , down from $111,000 a year earlier, selling coins bought at the higher price would realize a capital loss that could offset other capital gains. Stablecoins largely avoid these complexities, as tokens like USD Coin ( CRYPTO:USDC ) usually maintain a value close to $1. However, these transactions still count as disposals, and the IRS requires taxpayers to keep detailed records of every sale, exchange, or disposal of virtual currency and its fair market value. Mesh and Visa’s new setup benefits individuals who hold stablecoins, receive payments in them, or frequently make cross-border transactions and prefer to spend directly without cashing out first. Stablecoins simplify tax tracking and suit everyday purchases. However, long-term crypto holders may find it more advantageous to keep their investments separate and use a traditional card for payments. Tax tracking is the cost. Each purchase with a coin that has risen in value may create a gain to report. Small purchases add up fast over a year, so frequent spenders of appreciated coins will likely require tax software. If Mesh and its partners publish clear coin and fee lists at launch, this could become one of the easiest ways to spend crypto—as long as users know the tax owed on each transaction. Mesh has not yet specified which cryptocurrencies it will support, any applicable fees, or which countries it will include in the initial rollout.

extraction.body: In seconds, her financial security vanished behind a screen inside a gas station. Thousands of dollars deposited into a cryptocurrency ATM, in what one Johnston County woman thought was a payment to law enforcement for her safe release. But when the callers – impersonating local law enforcement – on the other end of the line requested an additional $4,000, she told them she simply didn’t have the money. That’s when the call dropped, and she realized she had been depleted of what she says was the entirety of her savings. “I just set up an appointment with a counselor, so I'd have somebody to talk to, because it's really hurt me financially and hurt me mentally." This victim, who wished to share her story with WRAL but not to be identified, is among thousands of victims across the country taken advantage of via a cryptocurrency kiosk. Public records out of Harnett County show a man recently lost more than $30,000 – which was described as 'almost all' of his savings – to a cryptocurrency machine. The machines – which upon first glance resemble regular ATMs – convert deposited cash into cryptocurrency investments. Rise of cryptocurrency crimes, and how kiosks can play a role Internet crimes facilitated through cryptocurrency kiosks are rising, following similar trends with general cryptocurrency related crimes. The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) began publicly reporting cryptocurrency kiosk metrics as of 2023. That year, the FBI received 5,500 complaints related to cryptocurrency kiosks, with losses of more than $189 million. Those numbers jumped in 2025, with the agency reporting 13,460 complaints totaling $389 million in victim losses. "Fraud losses at BTMs [Bitcoin ATMs] are skyrocketing, increasing nearly tenfold from 2020 to 2023," according to data cited from the Federal Trade Commission's (FTC) Consumer Sentinel Network. States are upping regulations, oversight over crypto ATMs. Many states are enacting tighter consumer regulations around cryptocurrency kiosks, including several who have imposed some kind of ban altogether. This year, North Carolina state lawmakers approved several regulatory changes to the Bitcoin ATM (BTM) industry by passing House Bill 920, introduced by State Rep. Jackson Some of the bill's language includes: Requiring licenses for all kiosk operators under the Money Transmissions Act. It stipulates that kiosk operators shall refund the "full dollar amount deposited" under certain conditions, including when someone reports a "fraudulent" transmission within 30 days. Although the bill's changes go into effect in 2027, Jackson questions – based on the level of fraud cases he's seen from this technology – if there is a legitimate reason to have any in the state in the first place. You don't have to do that through a gas station. There is no reason to go to one of these machines," he told WRAL. "Only a tiny percentage of those transactions are fraud," Tente told WRAL via email. Crypto deployers are highly unlikely to operate under such rules." State Rep. Tim Longest, D-Wake, previously expressed concern to WRAL about having the kiosks at all in the state. Longest, a consumer protection lawyer, said the bill's protections could have been stronger. "I think that we should really question whether these regulations go far enough and if these machines really serve any legitimate purpose," Rep. "You don't go to put cash in a machine and take out a stock, and yet a stock is exactly the same kind of speculative asset that cryptocurrency is." Attorney General Jackson alluded to the DOJ currently looking into cryptocurrency kiosk companies. "Investigation underway as we speak," Jackson said. WRAL reached out to several cryptocurrency kiosk companies operating in North Carolina, requesting information on how they plan to comply with new state laws. Below are responses from Byte Federal, through founder and chief compliance officer Mark Paolillo, and Chief Executive Officer, Paul Tarantino, as well as a marketing spokesperson for CoinFlip. They say many of the protections are already in place, independently, as part of their company's policies. Byte Federal: Most of HB 920's requirements match what we already do: scam warnings, blockchain analytics, live customer service, a written anti-fraud program, and dedicated compliance staff. We have advocated for a waiting period for first-time customers because it gives time to stop a scam before any funds leave. CoinFlip: CoinFlip already provides many of the consumer protections required under North Carolina’s new cryptocurrency kiosk law, including live customer support, scam warnings, and technology that screens for suspicious digital wallets. We appreciate the leadership of Representative Jackson and the collaborative efforts of stakeholders in developing a regulatory framework that strengthens consumer protections while preserving access to legitimate financial services. Question: Does the company plan to reduce its number of North Carolina kiosks? We are optimistic that NC lawmakers can see the error in the fee cap and make adjustments that allow legitimate kiosk operators to do business in the state.

extraction.body: In seconds, her financial security vanished behind a screen inside a gas station. Thousands of dollars deposited into a cryptocurrency ATM, in what one Johnston County woman thought was a payment to law enforcement for her safe release. But when the callers – impersonating local law enforcement – on the other end of the line requested an additional $4,000, she told them she simply didn’t have the money. That’s when the call dropped, and she realized she had been depleted of what she says was the entirety of her savings. “I just set up an appointment with a counselor, so I'd have somebody to talk to, because it's really hurt me financially and hurt me mentally." This victim, who wished to share her story with WRAL but not to be identified, is among thousands of victims across the country taken advantage of via a cryptocurrency kiosk. Public records out of Harnett County show a man recently lost more than $30,000 – which was described as 'almost all' of his savings – to a cryptocurrency machine. The machines – which upon first glance resemble regular ATMs – convert deposited cash into cryptocurrency investments. The transactions are virtually instant, difficult to trace and can be difficult to reverse. Internet crimes facilitated through cryptocurrency kiosks are rising, following similar trends with general cryptocurrency related crimes. The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) began publicly reporting cryptocurrency kiosk metrics as of 2023. That year, the FBI received 5,500 complaints related to cryptocurrency kiosks, with losses of more than $189 million. Those numbers jumped in 2025, with the agency reporting 13,460 complaints totaling $389 million in victim losses. "Fraud losses at BTMs [Bitcoin ATMs] are skyrocketing, increasing nearly tenfold from 2020 to 2023," according to data cited from the Federal Trade Commission's (FTC) Consumer Sentinel Network. Many states are enacting tighter consumer regulations around cryptocurrency kiosks, including several who have imposed some kind of ban altogether. This year, North Carolina state lawmakers approved several regulatory changes to the Bitcoin ATM (BTM) industry by passing House Bill 920, introduced by State Rep. Neal Jackson (R). "HB920 aims to protect North Carolinians from fraud through appropriate regulatory oversight while preserving our citizens ability to manage their finances. As technology advances, this legislation embraces innovation while ensuring consumers have the protections they deserve," says Rep. Jackson It stipulates that kiosk operators shall refund the "full dollar amount deposited" under certain conditions, including when someone reports a "fraudulent" transmission within 30 days. In an effort to reduce fraud, the bill also seeks to place limitations on transaction amounts, capping new customers at $2,000 daily for the first 30 days, and after that, at $5,000. North Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson believes the new customer limit may be the bill's most significant addition to protecting consumers. Although the bill's changes go into effect in 2027, Jackson questions – based on the level of fraud cases he's seen from this technology – if there is a legitimate reason to have any in the state in the first place. "We don't think there is any legitimate use for these devices. They are overwhelmingly used for fraud. If you want to invest in Bitcoin, you can do that without paying the 12% overhead. You don't have to do that through a gas station. If you want to send money to somebody, you can do that through a bank. There is no reason to go to one of these machines," he told WRAL. David Tente, the executive director of the ATM Industry Association, pushed back on Attorney General Jackson's assessment of how frequently the kiosks are used to facilitate crimes. "Only a tiny percentage of those transactions are fraud," Tente told WRAL via email. "Many of the [bill] requirements are similar to the bill Congress is working on. However, the 30-day return requirement makes everything else rather pointless. Crypto deployers are highly unlikely to operate under such rules." State Rep. Tim Longest, D-Wake, previously expressed concern to WRAL about having the kiosks at all in the state. Rep. Longest, a consumer protection lawyer, said the bill's protections could have been stronger. "I think that we should really question whether these regulations go far enough and if these machines really serve any legitimate purpose," Rep. Longest said. "You don't go to put cash in a machine and take out a stock, and yet a stock is exactly the same kind of speculative asset that cryptocurrency is." Attorney General Jackson alluded to the DOJ currently looking into cryptocurrency kiosk companies. "Investigation underway as we speak," Jackson said. WRAL reached out to several cryptocurrency kiosk companies operating in North Carolina, requesting information on how they plan to comply with new state laws. Below are responses from Byte Federal, through founder and chief compliance officer Mark Paolillo, and Chief Executive Officer, Paul Tarantino, as well as a marketing spokesperson for CoinFlip. They say many of the protections are already in place, independently, as part of their company's policies. Answers to questions are published in full for accuracy. Question: Which HB 920 changes will require you to update your kiosks? Byte Federal: Most of HB 920's requirements match what we already do: scam warnings, blockchain analytics, live customer service, a written anti-fraud program, and dedicated compliance staff. The changes we are implementing before January 1, 2027 include: CoinFlip: CoinFlip already provides many of the consumer protections required under North Carolina’s new cryptocurrency kiosk law, including live customer support, scam warnings, and technology that screens for suspicious digital wallets. We appreciate the leadership of Representative Jackson and the collaborative efforts of stakeholders in developing a regulatory framework that strengthens consumer protections while preserving access to legitimate financial services. CoinFlip has held a North Carolina money transmitter license since May 2024 and supports clear, consistent rules and accountability for all operators. We will implement the changes necessary to comply with the law’s requirements for when they take effect. Question: Does the company plan to reduce its number of North Carolina kiosks? Byte Federal: Complying with NC regulation is an easy lift for Byte Federal because we already meet the same standards in other states. The problem is the 12% fee cap, a regulation that puts legitimate operators running full compliance out of business in NC. We are optimistic that NC lawmakers can see the error in the fee cap and make adjustments that allow legitimate kiosk operators to do business in the state. CoinFlip: CoinFlip currently operates 152 kiosks across the state and has no plans to reduce its North Carolina kiosk network as a result of the new law.” Question: What is your policy for refunding scam victims? Byte Federal: We will comply fully with HB 920's refund provisions. Under the law, when the Commissioner of Banks determines a transaction was fraudulent and the victim reported it within 30 days, new customers receive a full refund and existing customers receive a refund of fees. That said, we believe the refund mandate holds compliant kiosk operators to a standard no other part of the financial system is held to. Byte Federal operates under the same federal framework as banks and other money transmitters: the Bank Secrecy Act, the USA PATRIOT Act's customer identification and due diligence rules, OFAC sanctions screening, and the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act's privacy and data-security requirements. Yet when a bank customer is tricked into sending a wire to a scammer, the bank generally does not refund that loss. Federal consumer protection rules for electronic transfers do not cover wire transfers. Wires instead fall under Article 4A of the Uniform Commercial Code, which relieves a bank of any refund obligation when it processed the customer's payment in good faith and followed agreed security procedures. Courts have applied this to scam victims directly. In one 2024 federal case, a customer who wired money to fraudulent crypto companies could not recover it from the bank, because the customer had authorized the wires and the bank had followed its procedures. A bitcoin transaction is just as irreversible as a wire. When a customer has passed identity verification, read our scam warnings, completed a verification call if they are 60 or older, and attested that they are sending funds to their own wallet without anyone directing them, we do not believe a compliant operator should be treated differently from a bank. The money in a kiosk is not the operators to give back, and the person responsible for the loss is the criminal who stole it. More broadly, we believe the most effective protection is stopping a scam before any money is sent. Once bitcoin is sent, it cannot be recalled by us or anyone else. That is why our program focuses on the moments before a transaction: the 60+ verification calls, attestations, wallet screening, and now the 48-hour new-customer hold, during which funds can still be returned. Outside the framework established by state law, we provide refunds where Byte Federal failed to follow its required compliance procedures. We also cooperate with law enforcement on every fraud report and provide transaction and wallet data to help trace and recover funds. CoinFlip: Our current policy provides transaction-fee refunds to confirmed scam victims. Identifying and stopping suspected scams before funds are transferred is critical when we hold a transaction before a transfer is complete; we can return it to the principal. Refund requests and reported scams are evaluated case by case, and our live support team helps customers report scams and request refunds. When a scam is reported, CoinFlip works with law enforcement to help stop or track scammers. Because blockchain transactions create a public record, investigators may be able to trace funds and, in some cases, assist with recovery. CoinFlip also blocks suspicious transactions and permanently blacklists high-risk digital wallet addresses, so they cannot be used at a CoinFlip kiosk again. We will honor the additional refund rights established by North Carolina’s new law when it takes effect.”

extraction.body: In seconds, her financial security vanished behind a screen inside a gas station. Thousands of dollars deposited into a cryptocurrency ATM, in what one Johnston County woman thought was a payment to law enforcement for her safe release. But when the callers – impersonating local law enforcement – on the other end of the line requested an additional $4,000, she told them she simply didn’t have the money. That’s when the call dropped, and she realized she had been depleted of what she says was the entirety of her savings. “I just set up an appointment with a counselor, so I'd have somebody to talk to, because it's really hurt me financially and hurt me mentally." This victim, who wished to share her story with WRAL but not to be identified, is among thousands of victims across the country taken advantage of via a cryptocurrency kiosk. Public records out of Harnett County show a man recently lost more than $30,000 – which was described as 'almost all' of his savings – to a cryptocurrency machine. The machines – which upon first glance resemble regular ATMs – convert deposited cash into cryptocurrency investments. Rise of cryptocurrency crimes, and how kiosks can play a role Internet crimes facilitated through cryptocurrency kiosks are rising, following similar trends with general cryptocurrency related crimes. The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) began publicly reporting cryptocurrency kiosk metrics as of 2023. That year, the FBI received 5,500 complaints related to cryptocurrency kiosks, with losses of more than $189 million. Those numbers jumped in 2025, with the agency reporting 13,460 complaints totaling $389 million in victim losses. "Fraud losses at BTMs [Bitcoin ATMs] are skyrocketing, increasing nearly tenfold from 2020 to 2023," according to data cited from the Federal Trade Commission's (FTC) Consumer Sentinel Network. States are upping regulations, oversight over crypto ATMs. Many states are enacting tighter consumer regulations around cryptocurrency kiosks, including several who have imposed some kind of ban altogether. This year, North Carolina state lawmakers approved several regulatory changes to the Bitcoin ATM (BTM) industry by passing House Bill 920, introduced by State Rep. Jackson Some of the bill's language includes: Requiring licenses for all kiosk operators under the Money Transmissions Act. It stipulates that kiosk operators shall refund the "full dollar amount deposited" under certain conditions, including when someone reports a "fraudulent" transmission within 30 days. Although the bill's changes go into effect in 2027, Jackson questions – based on the level of fraud cases he's seen from this technology – if there is a legitimate reason to have any in the state in the first place. You don't have to do that through a gas station. There is no reason to go to one of these machines," he told WRAL. "Only a tiny percentage of those transactions are fraud," Tente told WRAL via email. Crypto deployers are highly unlikely to operate under such rules." State Rep. Tim Longest, D-Wake, previously expressed concern to WRAL about having the kiosks at all in the state. Longest, a consumer protection lawyer, said the bill's protections could have been stronger. "I think that we should really question whether these regulations go far enough and if these machines really serve any legitimate purpose," Rep. "You don't go to put cash in a machine and take out a stock, and yet a stock is exactly the same kind of speculative asset that cryptocurrency is." Attorney General Jackson alluded to the DOJ currently looking into cryptocurrency kiosk companies. "Investigation underway as we speak," Jackson said. WRAL reached out to several cryptocurrency kiosk companies operating in North Carolina, requesting information on how they plan to comply with new state laws. Below are responses from Byte Federal, through founder and chief compliance officer Mark Paolillo, and Chief Executive Officer, Paul Tarantino, as well as a marketing spokesperson for CoinFlip. They say many of the protections are already in place, independently, as part of their company's policies. Byte Federal: Most of HB 920's requirements match what we already do: scam warnings, blockchain analytics, live customer service, a written anti-fraud program, and dedicated compliance staff. We have advocated for a waiting period for first-time customers because it gives time to stop a scam before any funds leave. CoinFlip: CoinFlip already provides many of the consumer protections required under North Carolina’s new cryptocurrency kiosk law, including live customer support, scam warnings, and technology that screens for suspicious digital wallets. We appreciate the leadership of Representative Jackson and the collaborative efforts of stakeholders in developing a regulatory framework that strengthens consumer protections while preserving access to legitimate financial services. Question: Does the company plan to reduce its number of North Carolina kiosks? We are optimistic that NC lawmakers can see the error in the fee cap and make adjustments that allow legitimate kiosk operators to do business in the state.

Question: Which HB 920 changes will require you to update your kiosks? Byte Federal: Most of HB 920's requirements match what we already do: scam warnings, blockchain analytics, live customer service, a written anti-fraud program, and dedicated compliance staff. The changes we are implementing before January 1, 2027 include: CoinFlip: CoinFlip already provides many of the consumer protections required under North Carolina’s new cryptocurrency kiosk law, including live customer support, scam warnings, and technology that screens for suspicious digital wallets. We appreciate the leadership of Representative Jackson and the collaborative efforts of stakeholders in developing a regulatory framework that strengthens consumer protections while preserving access to legitimate financial services. CoinFlip has held a North Carolina money transmitter license since May 2024 and supports clear, consistent rules and accountability for all operators. We will implement the changes necessary to comply with the law’s requirements for when they take effect. Question: Does the company plan to reduce its number of North Carolina kiosks? Byte Federal: Complying with NC regulation is an easy lift for Byte Federal because we already meet the same standards in other states. The problem is the 12% fee cap, a regulation that puts legitimate operators running full compliance out of business in NC. We are optimistic that NC lawmakers can see the error in the fee cap and make adjustments that allow legitimate kiosk operators to do business in the state. CoinFlip: CoinFlip currently operates 152 kiosks across the state and has no plans to reduce its North Carolina kiosk network as a result of the new law.” Question: What is your policy for refunding scam victims? Byte Federal: We will comply fully with HB 920's refund provisions. Under the law, when the Commissioner of Banks determines a transaction was fraudulent and the victim reported it within 30 days, new customers receive a full refund and existing customers receive a refund of fees. That said, we believe the refund mandate holds compliant kiosk operators to a standard no other part of the financial system is held to. Byte Federal operates under the same federal framework as banks and other money transmitters: the Bank Secrecy Act, the USA PATRIOT Act's customer identification and due diligence rules, OFAC sanctions screening, and the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act's privacy and data-security requirements. Yet when a bank customer is tricked into sending a wire to a scammer, the bank generally does not refund that loss. Federal consumer protection rules for electronic transfers do not cover wire transfers. Wires instead fall under Article 4A of the Uniform Commercial Code, which relieves a bank of any refund obligation when it processed the customer's payment in good faith and followed agreed security procedures. Courts have applied this to scam victims directly. In one 2024 federal case, a customer who wired money to fraudulent crypto companies could not recover it from the bank, because the customer had authorized the wires and the bank had followed its procedures. A bitcoin transaction is just as irreversible as a wire. When a customer has passed identity verification, read our scam warnings, completed a verification call if they are 60 or older, and attested that they are sending funds to their own wallet without anyone directing them, we do not believe a compliant operator should be treated differently from a bank. The money in a kiosk is not the operators to give back, and the person responsible for the loss is the criminal who stole it. More broadly, we believe the most effective protection is stopping a scam before any money is sent. Once bitcoin is sent, it cannot be recalled by us or anyone else. That is why our program focuses on the moments before a transaction: the 60+ verification calls, attestations, wallet screening, and now the 48-hour new-customer hold, during which funds can still be returned. Outside the framework established by state law, we provide refunds where Byte Federal failed to follow its required compliance procedures. We also cooperate with law enforcement on every fraud report and provide transaction and wallet data to help trace and recover funds. CoinFlip: Our current policy provides transaction-fee refunds to confirmed scam victims. Identifying and stopping suspected scams before funds are transferred is critical when we hold a transaction before a transfer is complete; we can return it to the principal. Refund requests and reported scams are evaluated case by case, and our live support team helps customers report scams and request refunds. When a scam is reported, CoinFlip works with law enforcement to help stop or track scammers. Because blockchain transactions create a public record, investigators may be able to trace funds and, in some cases, assist with recovery. CoinFlip also blocks suspicious transactions and permanently blacklists high-risk digital wallet addresses, so they cannot be used at a CoinFlip kiosk again. We will honor the additional refund rights established by North Carolina’s new law when it takes effect.”

In one 2024 federal case, a customer who wired money to fraudulent crypto companies could not recover it from the bank, because the customer had authorized the wires and the bank had followed its procedures. A bitcoin transaction is just as irreversible as a wire. When a customer has passed identity verification, read our scam warnings, completed a verification call if they are 60 or older, and attested that they are sending funds to their own wallet without anyone directing them, we do not believe a compliant operator should be treated differently from a bank. The money in a kiosk is not the operators to give back, and the person responsible for the loss is the criminal who stole it.

More broadly, we believe the most effective protection is stopping a scam before any money is sent. Once bitcoin is sent, it cannot be recalled by us or anyone else. That is why our program focuses on the moments before a transaction: the 60+ verification calls, attestations, wallet screening, and now the 48-hour new-customer hold, during which funds can still be returned. Outside the framework established by state law, we provide refunds where Byte Federal failed to follow its required compliance procedures. We also cooperate with law enforcement on every fraud report and provide transaction and wallet data to help trace and recover funds.

CoinFlip: Our current policy provides transaction-fee refunds to confirmed scam victims. Identifying and stopping suspected scams before funds are transferred is critical when we hold a transaction before a transfer is complete; we can return it to the principal. Refund requests and reported scams are evaluated case by case, and our live support team helps customers report scams and request refunds. When a scam is reported, CoinFlip works with law enforcement to help stop or track scammers. Because blockchain transactions create a public record, investigators may be able to trace funds and, in some cases, assist with recovery. CoinFlip also blocks suspicious transactions and permanently blacklists high-risk digital wallet addresses, so they cannot be used at a CoinFlip kiosk again. We will honor the additional refund rights established by North Carolina’s new law when it takes effect.”

The artificial intelligence (AI) revolution has produced two of the fastest-growing start-ups in history. OpenAI burst onto the scene in late 2022 when it launched ChatGPT, introducing consumers around the world to generative AI. Meanwhile, Anthropic has emerged as a formidable competitor with its Claude models. Both companies' growth has been extraordinary. Following a $122 billion funding round in March, OpenAI reached a valuation of $852 billion, while Anthropic was valued at $965 billion after its Series H round in May. Naturally, AI investors are eager to know when they can buy shares. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Anthropic confidentially filed for an initial public offering (IPO) in June and could make its public debut as soon as next month. OpenAI has also explored going public, although its timing remains uncertain. Here's an interesting alternative: Rather than waiting for either company to go public at a valuation approaching the trillion-dollar milestone, investors can buy Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG) instead. Alphabet stands to benefit regardless of which AI developer ultimately wins. Read on to learn why. One of Alphabet's quiet advantages is that it doesn't need its Gemini AI models to beat ChatGPT or Claude. That reason is Google Cloud provides compute infrastructure to its competitors. In May 2025, OpenAI agreed to use Google Cloud's capacity to train and deploy its AI models. This relationship is particularly interesting because up to that point, OpenAI was primarily tied to Microsoft Azure. Adding Google provided OpenAI with an alternative source of AI compute while giving Alphabet a hyperscaler customer whose infrastructure requirements are enormous. Anthropic's relationship with Google runs even deeper. In October 2025, Anthropic announced its use of Google's custom silicon, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). In April, this relationship was expanded to include multiple gigawatts of TPU capacity expected to come online in 2027. These arrangements create an attractive business model for Alphabet because the company can develop AI products for consumers while simultaneously supplying infrastructure that competing enterprises need. The strategy is already producing impressive results. During the second quarter, Google Cloud revenue surged 82% year over year to $24.8 billion. While not all of that growth came from OpenAI and Anthropic, their expanding infrastructure commitments underscore why Google Cloud should remain a major beneficiary of the AI boom. Alphabet isn't just an infrastructure partner to Anthropic. It's also one of the company's largest investors. Google initially invested in Anthropic in 2023. But by early 2026, Alphabet had invested roughly $3 billion in Anthropic and owned an estimated 14% equity stake. In April, Google announced plans to invest up to another $40 billion. The deal was structured to include an initial $10 billion commitment, with an additional $30 billion contingent on Anthropic meeting certain performance milestones. Why is Google investing so heavily in a company whose generative models compete directly with Gemini? The answer is simple: Alphabet is positioned to benefit from Anthropic's success in multiple ways. First, its equity investment will appreciate as Anthropic's valuation increases. Additionally, Anthropic is a major customer for Google's cloud infrastructure and custom AI chips. Third, Google's tie-up with Anthropic gives it exposure to an alternative AI ecosystem, reducing its dependence on Gemini emerging as the industry's go-to model. This is an unusually versatile position to be in. If Anthropic goes public at its reported $2 trillion valuation, a hypothetical 14% stake would be worth $280 billion. This shows how Alphabet can participate in one of the largest IPOs in history without investors needing to lift a finger and buy Anthropic stock directly. OpenAI's valuation of $852 billion represents approximately 17 times its reported $50 billion annualized revenue run rate. Meanwhile, Anthropic's $965 billion valuation represents 14 times its Q3 annualized revenue run rate of $67.2 billion. At a $2 trillion IPO valuation, Anthropic would trade at nearly 30 times its current revenue run rate. These are enormous premiums, especially considering the capital expenditures required to develop advanced AI. Moreover, OpenAI remains unprofitable while Anthropic recently reported a small profit on an adjusted operating basis. Alphabet offers a much different financial profile. During Q2, the company generated $120 billion in revenue and roughly $40.8 billion in operating income. Alphabet stock trades around a 23 times forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio -- a relatively reasonable valuation considering its established and highly profitable advertising and cloud businesses. The artificial intelligence (AI) revolution has produced two of the fastest-growing start-ups in history. OpenAI burst onto the scene in late 2022 when it launched ChatGPT, introducing consumers around the world to generative AI. Meanwhile, Anthropic has emerged as a formidable competitor with its Claude models.

Both companies' growth has been extraordinary. Following a $122 billion funding round in March, OpenAI reached a valuation of $852 billion, while Anthropic was valued at $965 billion after its Series H round in May. Naturally, AI investors are eager to know when they can buy shares.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Anthropic confidentially filed for an initial public offering (IPO) in June and could make its public debut as soon as next month. OpenAI has also explored going public, although its timing remains uncertain.

Here's an interesting alternative: Rather than waiting for either company to go public at a valuation approaching the trillion-dollar milestone, investors can buy Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG) instead. Alphabet stands to benefit regardless of which AI developer ultimately wins. Read on to learn why.

One of Alphabet's quiet advantages is that it doesn't need its Gemini AI models to beat ChatGPT or Claude. That reason is Google Cloud provides compute infrastructure to its competitors. In May 2025, OpenAI agreed to use Google Cloud's capacity to train and deploy its AI models.

This relationship is particularly interesting because up to that point, OpenAI was primarily tied to Microsoft Azure. Adding Google provided OpenAI with an alternative source of AI compute while giving Alphabet a hyperscaler customer whose infrastructure requirements are enormous.

Anthropic's relationship with Google runs even deeper. In October 2025, Anthropic announced its use of Google's custom silicon, called Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). In April, this relationship was expanded to include multiple gigawatts of TPU capacity expected to come online in 2027.

These arrangements create an attractive business model for Alphabet because the company can develop AI products for consumers while simultaneously supplying infrastructure that competing enterprises need.

The strategy is already producing impressive results. During the second quarter, Google Cloud revenue surged 82% year over year to $24.8 billion. While not all of that growth came from OpenAI and Anthropic, their expanding infrastructure commitments underscore why Google Cloud should remain a major beneficiary of the AI boom.

Alphabet isn't just an infrastructure partner to Anthropic. It's also one of the company's largest investors. Google initially invested in Anthropic in 2023. But by early 2026, Alphabet had invested roughly $3 billion in Anthropic and owned an estimated 14% equity stake. In April, Google announced plans to invest up to another $40 billion. The deal was structured to include an initial $10 billion commitment, with an additional $30 billion contingent on Anthropic meeting certain performance milestones.
Why is Google investing so heavily in a company whose generative models compete directly with Gemini?

The answer is simple: Alphabet is positioned to benefit from Anthropic's success in multiple ways. First, its equity investment will appreciate as Anthropic's valuation increases. Additionally, Anthropic is a major customer for Google's cloud infrastructure and custom AI chips. Third, Google's tie-up with Anthropic gives it exposure to an alternative AI ecosystem, reducing its dependence on Gemini emerging as the industry's go-to model.

This is an unusually versatile position to be in. If Anthropic goes public at its reported $2 trillion valuation, a hypothetical 14% stake would be worth $280 billion. This shows how Alphabet can participate in one of the largest IPOs in history without investors needing to lift a finger and buy Anthropic stock directly.

OpenAI's valuation of $852 billion represents approximately 17 times its reported $50 billion annualized revenue run rate. Meanwhile, Anthropic's $965 billion valuation represents 14 times its Q3 annualized revenue run rate of $67.2 billion. At a $2 trillion IPO valuation, Anthropic would trade at nearly 30 times its current revenue run rate.

These are enormous premiums, especially considering the capital expenditures required to develop advanced AI. Moreover, OpenAI remains unprofitable while Anthropic recently reported a small profit on an adjusted operating basis.

Alphabet offers a much different financial profile. During Q2, the company generated $120 billion in revenue and roughly $40.8 billion in operating income. Alphabet stock trades around a 23 times forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio -- a relatively reasonable valuation considering its established and highly profitable advertising and cloud businesses.

Data from on-chain analytics firm Glassnode indicates these profit-takers have driven significant inflows into exchanges, marking the largest movement onto trading platforms in a year—typically a sign that coins are about to be sold.

passages: Barclays has joined a growing list of UK banks imposing restrictions on crypto transactions after blocking its customers from purchasing cryptocurrencies with their credit cards.

The same paper also cited a YouGov survey which found that 14% of UK-based cryptocurrency investors had used some kind of credit card or credit facility to purchase crypto as of August 2024, up from 6% in August 2022.

Indeed, some UK banks—such as Barclays and Lloyds —have prevented transfers of any kind to Binance for several years now, while TSB and Santander have banned all crypto purchases since 2021 and 2022, respectively.

This crosses a line for some cryptocurrency experts, with analyst and author Glen Goodman telling Decrypt that, while he can sympathize with a bank stopping the use of credit for crypto purchases, he doesn’t think it’s right that it can stop someone from spending their own money.

Announcing the move on its Barclaycard website, Barclays said , “From 27 June 2025, we’ll block crypto-transactions made with a Barclaycard because we recognise there are certain risks with purchasing crypto-currencies.”

Outlining its concerns in a discussion paper , the FCA said, “We are concerned that consumers buying crypto assets with credit may take on unsustainable debt, particularly if the value of their crypto asset drops and they were relying on its value to repay.”
Barclays move comes after reports that the UK’s financial regulator, the Financial Conduct Authority, is seeking to introduce a blanket ban on all cryptocurrency purchases involving credit.

Announcing the move on its Barclaycard website, Barclays said , “From 27 June 2025, we’ll block crypto-transactions made with a Barclaycard because we recognise there are certain risks with purchasing crypto-currencies.” The bank went on to explain that it has imposed the block because a decline in cryptocurrency prices could land its customers in debt, while adding that digital assets aren’t covered by existing banking and financial protections. Barclays move comes after reports that the UK’s financial regulator, the Financial Conduct Authority, is seeking to introduce a blanket ban on all cryptocurrency purchases involving credit. Outlining its concerns in a discussion paper , the FCA said, “We are concerned that consumers buying crypto assets with credit may take on unsustainable debt, particularly if the value of their crypto asset drops and they were relying on its value to repay.” The same paper also cited a YouGov survey which found that 14% of UK-based cryptocurrency investors had used some kind of credit card or credit facility to purchase crypto as of August 2024, up from 6% in August 2022. Barclays decision to stop its customers using their credit cards for cryptocurrency transactions also comes after similar moves by Chase UK, HSBC and Nationwide in 2023 . In Nationwide’s case, it set a £5,000 (approximately $6,860) spending limit on crypto payments using debit cards, which come directly from a customer’s checking account. Going even further, Chase UK prevented its customers from making any kind of transaction to cryptocurrency exchanges and services, whether from a customer’s credit or debit card. This crosses a line for some cryptocurrency experts, with analyst and author Glen Goodman telling Decrypt that, while he can sympathize with a bank stopping the use of credit for crypto purchases, he doesn’t think it’s right that it can stop someone from spending their own money. “If Barclaycard doesn't want to lend money to crypto traders, that's up to them,” he said. “They need to manage their own risk as they see fit, and they make a good point that crypto losses are never covered by the financial services compensation scheme.” However, Goodman added that it really “annoys” him when UK banks refuse to let people send their own money from their own bank account to a crypto trading account. “And that happens more often than you might think," he adds. Indeed, some UK banks—such as Barclays and Lloyds —have prevented transfers of any kind to Binance for several years now, while TSB and Santander have banned all crypto purchases since 2021 and 2022, respectively. Despite regarding such actions as examples of overreach, Goodman does caution against using debt to trade cryptocurrency, given the risks involved.
